# Native JIT implementation plan

## Status and intent

- **Status:** implementation in progress on `feat/native-jit`; no release acceptance yet.
- **Planned against:** commit `47b34de`, Luna `0.5.1`, 2026-09-30.
- **Priority:** architecture/performance; correctness and execution control take precedence over speed.
- **Risk:** high; generated machine code introduces a new trusted, unsafe execution boundary.
- **Effort:** a substantial, plausibly multi-month compiler/runtime project. Estimates must be revised after the first integrated native slice is measured.
- **Requested artifact:** this root-level `PLAN_JIT.md`; no separate plan index is required.

### Phase-reused VM progress — measured and rejected, 2026-10-19

The historical unified-progress trial is not being replayed: it nested the
original interpreter publisher in a larger wrapper with a second destructor.
The new model stores either in-flight native progress or the final report in
one enum occupying the original `Option<u32>` storage. Its total-dispatch field
can serve as VM progress until finishing; one destructor publishes only the
interpreted partition, at the original boundary and through the original
manager borrow. No extra allocation, cached policy, batched publication or
unsafe code is introduced.

Layout checks require the phase enum and complete guard to match the old report
and guard sizes, and the historical wrapper to be larger. Independent comparisons
against the unchanged publisher cover 378 saturation/partition/report scenarios,
terminal adjustments, native prefixes, rollback, typed unwinding, held-manager
refusal and full-width counters. State transitions compute their results before
mutating fields, preserving unwinding publication if a checked build traps.

The original runtime was active during the initial test-only model. Model plus
existing statistics/native/heap checks pass **55 checks / six summaries**, zero
failures/ignored checks; the refined model passes **four / one summary**. Integration
`bd4064f` uses the guard's dispatch field as the loop-progress counter, preserving
terminal adjustments and provisional rollback without changing break scopes.
Formatting/check-all and **61 focused checks / ten summaries** pass with zero
failures/ignored checks. All original performance/resource/platform/release requirements stay
open. Work stays on `feat/native-jit`, without new branches or worktrees.
Evidence: `target/jit-evidence/hook-resume-recovery/phase-progress/`.

Native-prefix/region validation adds **79 checks / ten summaries / two ignored**,
with no failures. Fresh baseline builds at test-only-model commit `0f09818`
reproduce all six original `218112b` images byte-for-byte. Candidate `bd4064f`
changes all six image hashes, including no-feature images after the VM source
edit; that difference is recorded, not represented as identity or waived from
comparison.

Three whole-execution profile families cover native callbacks and compiled-Off /
no-feature float loops in both profiles: **24 alternating processes / 120 execute
calls / 48 warmups**. Printed callback statistics match; image/object identity,
all 13 event totals and full text-symbol partitions reconcile. Each family
accepts two valid and rejects four identity-corruption fixtures. Float diagnostics
attribute the VM and the full image, not a selected subset of whole-workload work.

No-feature float counts remain identical: **4,081,046** speed and **4,375,155**
shipping. Compiled-Off float counts fall **4,015,310 → 3,936,535** and
**4,109,344 → 4,033,702** respectively. Actual native callbacks increase
**9,438,782 → 9,448,784** in speed and **11,684,260 → 11,754,274** in shipping.
The callback cost is retained, not hidden behind the interpreter saving. These
are modeled instruction counts, not a measured speedup or original-gate pass.
Full Force validation passes **2,048 executions / 91 summaries**, zero failures
and **23 ignored**. Configured Stacked/Tree Miri each pass **19 checks / six

### Native slot-conversion call boundary — measured and rejected, 2026-10-19

**Resumed by the user on `feat/native-jit`.** The previously interrupted
validation output is preserved and is not claimed as a full test pass or
performance result. The conversion candidates are tested and reverted
on the existing implementation branch. Initial validation uses the retained detached
source snapshot only after confirming its runtime, test and build inputs match;
no local/remote branch or additional worktree is created.
Experimental branch names below are historical provenance: **59 local and 55
remote trial/experiment branches have been removed**. Only `main`, `develop` and
`feat/native-jit` remain locally and on origin. Their prior tips are preserved in
a verified local Git bundle; `.git/branch-cleanup-latest` identifies its directory.
Source/evidence worktrees are retained detached, without trial branches. Future
work uses the existing implementation branch; creating additional branches
requires an explicit user request, as recorded in root `AGENTS.md`.

A current exact-image audit decodes every executed instruction in the original
`218112b` seven-register native transport. Twenty captured callback executions
retain all warmups across two control processes and both profiles. Independent
symbol totals reconcile; the parser checks captured launch-object/image identity,
linker range and instruction coverage. Each profile accepts valid/restored
fixtures and rejects seven wrong-hash/object/range/disassembly/count/event cases.
No new timing or hardware-counter capture is claimed.

Steady transport self work is **1,560,341 instructions in speed / 1,580,358 in
shipping**. Shipping executes **35,007 direct calls to `Slot::value`** and
**5,001 direct calls to `record_native_exit`**, alongside 5,001 indirect native
entry calls. These targets are resolved from the exact loaded image's linker map,
not guessed from stripped disassembly names. Speed conversion is already inlined.
The explicit stack-operand counts are not stack traffic attributable solely to
conversion and are not a claim of removable time.

Initial candidate `eb25372` forces the existing `Slot::value` conversion inline,
without integer/reference shortcuts, skipped writebacks, narrowed counters,
changed tags, altered ABI or retained pointers. Unlike earlier rejected scalar
specializations, its hypothesis is removing the shipping aggregate-return call
boundary while retaining the exact match body. Previous projection outlining,
static import/writeback masks, counter publishing and callback handoffs are not
reintroduced. Baseline ABI validation passes **10 checks**. Resumed formatting,
all-feature checking and broad JIT validation pass **1,479 checks / 11 summaries**,
with zero failures and **22 ignored**. The full all-target Force suite completes
with **2,044 passing checks / 91 summaries / 23 ignored**, zero failures. The
six production images build, retaining byte-identical no-feature controls. Actual
native callback profiles and their two positive/four identity-corruption fixtures
complete, with all 13 events and full symbol partitions reconciled. The proposed
boundary removal **does not occur**: speed stays at **9,438,782** whole-execution
instructions and shipping stays at **11,684,260**. Shipping loses the 315,062-
instruction `Slot::value` symbol but gains a 390,077-instruction `Slot::write_back`
symbol; transport self work drops by exactly 75,015. This is relocated work, not
a performance improvement, and does not justify a timing campaign for that form.

The refinement also forces the existing outer `write_back` method inline. It
keeps the exact conversion body and tests on `feat/native-jit`, without creating
branches or additional worktrees. A plain `git archive` source snapshot provides
immutable provenance for diagnostic profiling before repeating expensive broad
gates. Full Force/Miri/fallback and original repeated elapsed gates remain
required before retaining the refinement; reordering diagnostics is not a waiver.
Refinement `729c697` passes formatting/check-all and **68 focused checks / five
summaries**, zero failures/ignored checks. All six production images and actual
callback profiles verify, including printed counter/resource parity and the
identity-corruption fixtures. Both no-feature images remain byte-identical to
their original controls. No out-of-line `Slot::value` or `Slot::write_back`
symbol remains in the shipping image. Whole steady callback work falls from
**11,684,260 to 11,509,225 instructions** in shipping, but grows from **9,438,782
to 9,463,787** in speed. This is a mixed result, not a claimed speedup or evidence
that the speed callback gate is solved. The larger serial campaign completes:
full Force, both Miri borrow models, real i686 fallback, then both original

The refined source passes full Force **2,044 / 91 summaries / 23 ignored**, both

Two original elapsed screens complete **288 commands / 28,512 native executions /

### Independent interpreter-counter publication — measured and rejected, 2026-10-19

Unlike the rejected direct statistics-cell-reference trial, `fd4071a` removes
the manager borrow from interpreter-guard publication. Three `Cell<u64>` counters
live in the existing charged runtime owner, separately from the cache/configuration
`RefCell`. Each guard still publishes at its original Drop boundary; no frame,
callback, error or suspension boundary is batched away. Public snapshots merge
these counters with manager-owned native/pair counts using saturating addition.
There is no extra allocation, unsafe code, retained GC pointer or cached mode.

The owner grows **24 bytes**, explicitly included in `HeaderCharge` and checked
against the previous owner layout. No zero-cost resource claim is made. Two
independent counter models (`7ad6fca`) cover interleaved updates, saturation and
non-consuming snapshots; the unchanged-runtime baseline passes **53 checks /
six summaries**. The activated candidate passes **110 checks / 17 summaries**,
zero ignored, including public dispatch, native/heap, nested guards, typed panic
unwinding, callback observations, owner quotas and reclamation.

One private behavior deliberately changes with the storage separation: publishing
interpreter counts no longer conflicts with a borrowed cache/config manager.
The old panic assertion is replaced by exact publication and unchanged manager
storage checks under both shared and mutable manager borrows. Public snapshot
borrowing and all counter/value assertions remain. Test-only resets clear both
stores; internal trace readers now observe the merged snapshot. This is not an
unchecked bypass of a borrow on the same storage.

The first full Force run stops at **1,492 passing / one failing / 23 ignored**
library tests: the atomic-call oracle still compares manager-only storage after
interpreter counts move out of it. `fc0d660` releases that manager borrow and
compares the merged snapshot, retaining every expected value. It also extends
the independent-publication fixture to typed unwinding while the manager is
mutably borrowed. Refined focused validation passes **111 checks / 18 summaries**,
zero ignored; the failed full-run logs and source revision remain preserved.

The refined candidate completes full all-target Force validation: **2,047 passing
checks / 91 summaries / 23 ignored**, with no failures. The ignored tests are not
claimed as executed coverage. All six default-flag production images build and
verify; both no-feature images remain byte-identical to the original controls.

Whole-execution profiles complete for compiled-Off `closure_upvalue` and actual
native-benchmark Auto `rust_callbacks`, each using eight alternating processes,
40 execute calls including 16 warmups, and both speed/shipping profiles. Loaded
image identity, all 13 event totals and full symbol partitions reconcile; each
profile family passes two positive and four deliberate identity-corruption
fixtures. Printed callback counters/resources match exactly, without dropping
fields. The separately validated 24-byte runtime-owner charge is not printed by
this benchmark and is not claimed to be unchanged.

Compiled-Off upvalues reduce instructions attributed to the executable from
**15,979,740 to 15,919,737** in speed and **17,620,113 to 17,360,101** in shipping,
consistently across all captured calls. External-library counts remain included
in the reconciled whole-execution totals, not silently discarded. Native callback
steady executions are mixed: whole-execution counts change **9,438,782 to
9,448,783** in speed (10,001 more), and **11,684,260 to 11,654,249** in shipping
(30,011 fewer). A disappearing Drop helper alone would overstate the shipping
savings because some work moves into the VM. These instruction results justify
elapsed evaluation of the compiled-Off gap, not a claimed callback speedup.

Both Miri borrow models now pass **40 checks / 14 summaries** each (ten nonempty
summaries); real i686 fallback passes **50 checks / 19 summaries** (14 nonempty).
All have zero failures/ignored checks, explicit positive matches for the new
counter models, borrowed-manager publication, atomic saturation, charged-owner
layout and exact-ceiling/unwind cases. Miri and i686 do not establish generated
native-code execution. Both repeated original elapsed screens complete with
**288 commands / 28,512 native executions / 570,240 feature-cost iterations**,
zero printed counter/resource mismatches, unchanged original thresholds and
all nine workloads on CPUs 0/16. Each auditor accepts valid/restored evidence
and rejects all 13 deliberate corruptions. No owned builds/tests/profilers
overlap timing. Capture/audit exit zero is not a passing performance gate.

The compiled-Off shipping upvalue target improves modestly: control/trial median
ratios are **1.013410 / 1.025234** on CPU0 and **1.009275 / 1.011832** on CPU16.
But CPU0 shipping integer ratios are **0.880594 / 0.898874**, and float ratios

Their A/B placebo medians remain near one; the second screen retains all noisy

Candidate original speed-native gates fail **19/96** in each screen, and
compiled-Off gates fail **33/216**, then **32/216**. The small target gain does

The isolated branch is `trial/jit-interpreter-counter-root`; main runtime is
unchanged. This candidate's focused safety/profile/elapsed runs are terminal;

### Common Lua-state prefix — measured and rejected, 2026-10-19

The completed long prepared-table campaigns' unchanged-control observations
place speed callback Off/Auto medians near **0.8142 / 0.8178** on CPU0/16,
below the original **1/1.2** minimum. Compiled-Off upvalue medians are about
**1.0877 / 1.2121** in shipping, above the original **1.05** ceiling. These
pooled contended observations prioritize remaining gaps; they are not new gates
or evidence of a candidate improvement.

A baseline-only layout diagnostic (`9f9615a`) passes with and without JIT. It
confirms that enabling the feature shifts every shared `State` field by **16
bytes**: ordinary state is **128 bytes**, JIT state **144 bytes**. Isolated trial
`14ed51c` gives the private state an explicit C field order and places the two
optional JIT handles after the common fields. This preserves shared-field
offsets across feature builds without padding the interpreter-only state,
changing `Value` representation, adding allocations/caches/unsafe code, or
changing initialization order. Derived GC tracing still covers all fields;
its traversal order changes and must be validated rather than assumed harmless.

Both layouts retain their original total sizes. Four candidate layout checks
pass across the feature choices, including a common-prefix assertion; baseline
diagnostics pass twice. This tests feature-dependent data layout, not another
function/branch alignment policy or an established explanation for the slowdown.
Focused validation now passes **198 executions / 32 summaries**, zero failures
or ignored tests, including configuration, memory limits, hooks and GC requests.
All six exact production images build and verify. Both no-feature executables
are **byte-identical to the frozen controls**; flags/configurations/environments
match. Candidate diagnostic output verifies equal common-field offsets across
feature choices. Full Force validation now passes **2,046 executions / 91
summaries**, zero failures and **23 ignored**. Fresh-target Stacked/Tree Miri
each pass **18 checks**, covering both feature choices for state layout, hook
resumption and memory-limit behavior; emitted warnings remain in the logs.
Real i686-musl passes **24 checks** across layout, hooks, memory and fallback.
Zero-case workspace summaries are not counted as test executions. These are
Rust-state/fallback checks, not native execution under Miri/i686 or complete
platform certification.

Both original elapsed campaigns now finish **288 commands / 28,512 native
executions / 570,240 cost iterations**, after all owned validation work. Full
native counter/resource records match, source/image/tool witnesses verify, and
each audit rejects all 13 corruption fixtures. All contention and outliers remain.
These terminal-zero audit/capture statuses are not passing performance gates.

Reject this runtime change. CPU0 shipping compiled-Off integer control/trial
ratios are **0.924502 / 0.906888**, float **0.895598 / 0.850165**, approximately
**8–10% / 12–18% longer elapsed time**. Corresponding median A/B controls stay
near one. CPU16 shipping upvalue Off ratios **0.980619 / 0.979056** worsen the
targeted overhead rather than remove it. CPU0 speed callback ratios improve
**1.019269 / 1.008399**, but shipping callbacks instead give **0.989714 /
0.974384**. Preserving common state offsets is therefore not a sufficient remedy

The runtime and layout fixtures remain isolated on `trial/jit-state-core-prefix`;

### Non-fall-through block alignment — rejected, 2026-10-19

Current hardware evidence motivates a distinct, fixed compiler-policy experiment:
`RUSTFLAGS='-C llvm-args=-align-all-nofallthru-blocks=5'`. Pinned rustc 1.97.1 /
LLVM 22.1.6 advertises this option as log2 alignment of blocks without fall-through
predecessors, avoiding padding on fall-through execution paths. This is not the
previous whole-VM 4K placement or branch-crossing policy, not an offset sweep,
and not a change to Cranelift's generated native-code alignment. No default flag
or runtime change is promoted.

The frozen source is `218112b`, identical to the timed control. Current main's
production `src` remains identical, excluding the independent test-only
prepared-key fixtures. All six new production images build and pass workload
smoke checks at the existing shared builder/target. Source/configuration/hash
witnesses verify, with the declared flag the sole retained environment difference.
Full original nine-case, CPU0/16, speed/shipping comparisons and their
controls remain required; smaller instruction-delivery counts alone cannot
establish acceptance. A static direct-target parser passes six positive and six
negative fixtures, including duplicate/indirect/external targets and incomplete,
overlapping or mid-instruction targets. It does not classify block hotness or
prove all branch targets require alignment.

Static VM disassembly verifies complete instruction coverage in all four images.
Speed VM extent grows **55,274 → 71,333 bytes**, shipping **42,104 → 57,061**;
unique internal direct targets stay **952 / 745**, while targets on 32-byte
boundaries rise **43 → 495 / 34 → 376**. These counts include cold blocks and
do not establish dynamic instruction savings.

Both elapsed campaigns now finish **288 commands / 28,512 native executions /
570,240 cost iterations**, with matching complete native counter/resource records,
verified source/image/tool witnesses and all 13 corruption fixtures rejected per
audit. No owned build/test/profiler overlaps measurement. All external contention
and outliers remain; terminal-zero capture/audit statuses are not passing gates.

Reject the policy. CPU0 shipping compiled-Off integer control/candidate ratios
are **0.735378 / 0.818875**, float **0.709204 / 0.819659**, adverse in six then
five of six rounds for each workload. Corresponding A/B medians stay between
**0.996813 and 1.002013**. This is approximately **22–36% / 22–41% longer
elapsed time**, not a fix. CPU16 shipping float also loses in all six rounds of
each campaign (**0.961197 / 0.969500**). CPU0 shipping callback gains
**1.027100 / 1.024900** do not compensate. No-feature numeric results vary
substantially between CPU0 campaigns and remain recorded rather than normalized
away. Candidate speed-native gate failures are **21 then 23 / 96**, cost
**34 then 51 / 216**. These counts do not cancel individual regressions.

The fixed alignment policy increases VM code size about **29% / 36%** and fails
the end-to-end comparison. No flag or runtime change is promoted. This excluded
compiler policy does not identify the hardware cause or justify another offset
search. No full Force, Miri or cross-platform certification is claimed for this
rejected experiment; full native-JIT acceptance remains incomplete.

Evidence: `target/jit-evidence/hook-resume-recovery/block-target-align/`.

### Native closed-upvalue helper — measured trials, 2026-10-19

Current callback attribution motivates a private JIT helper change, not another
VM operand rewrite. First-stage `fb22491` forces `Frame::upvalue` inline. Sixty
focused helper/native/heap/upvalue executions pass, but fresh instruction profiles
show most work merely moves to a now-outlined `get_upvalue_with`: speed callback
totals **9,448,381 → 9,433,381**, shipping **11,678,795 → 11,658,795**. Disappearance
of the original helper symbol is not an 80,000/85,000-instruction saving.

Refinement `6a06213`, formatted in `f557ebc`, reads the current upvalue state in
the private helper, returns `Closed(value)` directly and retains the original
canonical resolver for `Open` cells, including current-frame scratch aliases.
There is no cached cell state, unsafe code, new storage, relaxed bounds check,
changed counter or shared interpreter-method annotation. The first build stops
at formatting before compilation; its failed logs remain. After repository-native
formatting, all **60 focused executions / six summaries** pass with zero failures
or ignored tests. Both candidates' no-feature production images are byte-identical
to the frozen controls; flags, configuration and environment match.

Each stage captures **eight processes / 40 whole-execute calls / 16 warmups**,
alternating frozen control and candidate Auto images in speed/shipping. All
13 exclusive events and full text-symbol partitions reconcile; both parsers
accept valid records and reject wrong image hashes/loaded paths. Each worker
verifies the result and **99,375 native instructions**. Measured totals repeat
exactly within each image/profile. The refinement reduces speed totals to
**9,383,381** and shipping to **11,603,795**, approximately **0.69% / 0.64%** less
work. VM and native transport self work are unchanged. These are instruction
reductions, **not elapsed speedups or performance acceptance**.

Full Force validation of the refinement now passes **2,044 executions / 91
summaries**, zero failures and **23 ignored**. Matched native benchmark images
and two complete elapsed campaigns finish **288 commands / 28,512 native
executions / 570,240 cost iterations**. Full counter/resource records match;
both audits reject all 13 corruption fixtures. No owned build/test/profiler
overlaps timing. CPU0 speed callback control/trial ratios are **1.026247 /
1.010922**, while shipping callbacks give **0.992509 / 0.992738**. CPU16 speed
callbacks give **0.997211 / 1.005904**, shipping **0.982621 / 0.993871**. CPU0
speed array Auto initially gives **0.956599** without a repeated greater-than-2%
adverse median. Large favorable repeat excursions also remain unaccepted as
causal gains. Candidate speed native failures are **nine then 13 / 96**, cost
failures **48 then 54 / 216**; fewer aggregate failures do not prove acceptance.

Both trials are committed/pushed on separate branches; main runtime is unchanged.
Mixed elapsed evidence motivates a third, **201-native-sample** campaign retaining
the same images, all nine cases, CPUs, rotated controls and original thresholds;
cost comparisons remain at 11 samples / 20 iterations. It now completes **144

the cause of all timing changes. A follow-up tests refusing each missing numeric
operand immediately, before constructing the two-numeric-value sum. Both reads
are side-effect-free; the Get opcode and all subsequent canonical fallback
effects must retain their original ordering. Evidence:
`target/jit-evidence/hook-resume-recovery/vm-upvalue-numeric/`.

rather than increase, and branch misses were unchanged in the first capture.

order-of-magnitude change. Local perf event descriptions are retained.

This is evidence of an instruction-delivery problem in the exact diagnostic
image, not proof of a particular basic-block, cache-set or alignment cause.
Inspect the hot machine-code layout before selecting another runtime change;

### PC-and-budget binding prototype — not promoted, 2026-10-18

Test-only `RequireBoundBudget(pc, budget)` composes the PC specialization with

body. Both guards must pass; other inputs decline through the original
Interpreter exit without changing slots or charging source instructions.
Bindings0..64 are supported; larger bindings are rejected. The public native
adapter still clamps supplied budgets to64. A raw-entry fixture separately
verifies rejection of unclamped65/high-bit/maximum inputs, so adapter clamping
cannot hide an incorrect machine-code guard. Production selection is unchanged.

passes its inverse preservation oracle; structural and expansion checks run
after composition. This retains the earlier test-only, uncharged clone/string
workspace limitation. All ordinary integer-loop and prepared-helper passes
remain enabled. No binding is installed into the runtime cache.

### Queued callback handoff — measured and withdrawn, 2026-10-18

Trial `cb720ba` carried one already-queued callback between feature-JIT executor
iterations. Extraction happens only after the original step fuel charge and
continuation check; exhausted/interrupted steps leave the frame canonical.
Running/deferred-error threads, other frame kinds and unavailable borrows retain
the original dispatch. The next iteration consumes the callback through the
existing callback branch, without repeating thread-mode classification or its
frame pop. No values, native pointers or stack borrows are retained across user
code, suspension or a return from `Executor::step`.

This differs from the rejected second-mode-query elision and callback activation
borrow fusion. It also adds an end-of-step inspection on non-callback paths;
that cost may outweigh the saving. There is no performance acceptance yet.

independent chained-callback fixture passes both feature builds across eleven
fuel budgets and both initial/in-callback interruption choices. It verifies
callback-visible frames/borrows, exact fuel, queued frames at interruption,
minimum progress and results. The eligibility fixture checks all running,
deferred-error, error-taken and queued/not-queued combinations.

and allocation totals also increase in both rounds, with their variable amounts
retained. Miri passes the two handoff fixtures and four existing mode fixtures
under both Stacked seed90 and Tree seed91 (39 warnings per invocation).

### Callback stack offset overflow — corrected, 2026-10-18

Investigation of cross-callback import reuse found that callback stack suffix
isolation was not valid for all public indices. Six new regressions fail on the
unchanged runtime with arithmetic overflow checks disabled: relative additions
in get, set, remove, sub_stack and resize wrap into the caller prefix, and drain
endpoint arithmetic admits an invalid wrapped range. This is a runtime boundary
defect, not evidence that register caching is ready to enable.

`9a36800` uses checked additions without changing the Value representation,
canonical stack type, native ABI or public raw-stack handles. Overflowing get
and remove return Nil/None; set, sub_stack, resize and drain reject overflow
before mutation. Seven unit tests cover prefix preservation, normal suffix-vector
behavior and **847 drain-bound combinations** against independent u128 arithmetic.
An integrated callback test preserves caller scalar/table locals through repeated
calls, caught errors, native reentry and collection between executions.

- Formatting/check-all and **46 focused executions / 12 summaries** pass with
  overflow checks disabled, including no-feature/Off/Auto/Force callback runs
  and existing drain/consume/replace contracts.
- Optimized release (`opt-level=s`, LTO) passes **14 bounds executions**, seven
  without JIT and seven with JIT.
- Stacked seed 82 and Tree seed 83 each pass seven no-feature bounds tests in
  Miri, with 18 warnings each. Miri does not execute generated native code.
- The normal-profile no-feature workspace/all-target/doc suite plus JIT heap
  and upvalue suites pass **500 executions / 90 summaries**. The full sequence
  also passes **500 / 90** with arithmetic overflow checks disabled after the
  independent test-oracle correction below. The retained-public-stack-alias
  regression passes in both, preserving its required native reentry.

The first broad wrapping-arithmetic run exposed an unrelated return-span oracle
assumption: `debug_assertions` was treated as the arithmetic-overflow setting.
An isolated unchanged `bed263d` checkout reproduces the identical fuel mismatch
(-5 versus -4). Production return handling eagerly evaluates `len - start` in
`unwrap_or`; whether that panics is controlled by overflow checks, not the debug
assertion flag. Test-only `563d5fe` probes arithmetic behavior instead. Its four
explicit no-feature/JIT × checked/wrapping lanes pass. No production fuel or
return-order change is made; both original failed logs remain retained.

This is a correctness repair, **not a performance improvement or full native
release acceptance**. No elapsed campaign or platform/resource acceptance is
claimed for the fix. Future import reuse must still account for retained public
stack handles and OpenUpValue handles, even after a thread's current open-upvalue
list becomes empty. Internal-write-only versioning remains insufficient.
Evidence and the unchanged baseline worktree are under
`target/jit-evidence/hook-resume-recovery/stack-bounds/`; reproduction targets are
`stack-bounds`, `stack-bounds-miri`, `stack-bounds-callbacks` and `vm-return-spans`.

`933a9c9` adds a separate `jit_cycles` diagnostic example without changing the

confirmed the framing; the corrected reader accepts newline-only and optionally
NUL-terminated acknowledgements across multiple windows, while rejecting leading
or repeated NULs, malformed/truncated replies and write failures. Workload errors
still send disable. Failed initial captures remain excluded from results.

All seven frozen workloads pass Off/Auto smoke runs with no compilation during
collection. The callback campaign then completes **16 captures**, four alternating
Off/Auto rounds on each of CPUs 0 and 16, with **10,000 verified executions** per

report headers, weighted event totals, zero lost samples and host/native address
ranges. Each of 25 counters equals 10,000 times its independent single-execution
control; Auto executes **200,070,000 native logical instructions** per capture,
versus zero Off. No compiler symbols appear in the warmed samples. Source and
image manifests verify before/after; no owned build, test or second profiler
overlaps a capture. External contention and all per-run observations are retained.

| Auto user-cycle self share | CPU 0 | CPU 16 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| VM slice | 18.86% | 20.47% |
| Executor | 19.50% | 20.34% |
| Seven-slot native entry | 11.70% | 10.57% |
| Prepared-key helper | 11.02% | 13.16% |
| Named generated code | 5.54% | 5.91% |

The original whole-process attribution is no longer the only evidence for
prioritizing entry/helper costs over tiny arithmetic-guard rewrites. All sampled
addresses in the four selected host functions also match decoded instruction

Sampling skid prevents interpreting an individual address as instruction latency.
These shares do not prove a speedup, identify a causal hardware bottleneck, or

linked diagnostic image is not asserted byte-identical to a shipping benchmark.

Reproduction uses `make jit-cycles-tests`, `make jit-cycles-build`, and

**400,075 / 400,080**; the explicit `%rsp` memory operands account for all of

and the totals agree with independent Callgrind annotation. Eight valid profile
checks and three refusal checks pass: missing assembly, wrong-image assembly

traffic, not hardware cache misses or a causal elapsed-time regression.

### VM-entry hook continuation trial — 2026-10-18

Trial `5a1a25c` restores the ordinary VM call signature: the executor retains
the frame-owned `HookResume` marker until VM entry, rather than passing a
separate resumption boolean through a wrapper. The VM consumes the marker only
after the zero-instruction-budget check. It still skips exactly the already
delivered hook, preserves the native-activation barrier, and uses the existing
frame allocation. No context-global continuation flag is introduced.

Boundary tests committed separately as `7d19825` establish the new internal
entry contract: repeated zero-budget entries preserve the marker, PC, fuel and
interruption state; the next instruction consumes it without growing frame
capacity; subsequent hooks are delivered normally. The new marker-entry test
fails against the old entry API while its ordinary-entry control passes. This
is a changed internal contract, not a newly discovered user-facing defect.

Formatting/all-feature checks and **77 focused test executions** pass. All

### Progress snapshot — 2026-10-13

#### Hook instruction resumption — count-one starvation corrected

The separate hook finding from the policy trial has a bounded standalone
reproducer (`a368697`, `make hook-progress`). On the unchanged no-feature VM,
1,000 executor steps at fuel one fire the Rust hook **500 times** without
finishing the first instruction. Hook calls leave the originating PC unchanged;
returning retried hook delivery before executing that same instruction.

Fix `0e4d600` gives a successful hook return its own frame-owned resumption
marker. The executor consumes it and runs a specialization of the common VM
that skips only the first hook check. Ordinary instruction execution, errors,
fuel accounting and subsequent hook checks remain in the shared implementation.
Normal VM entry uses the constant-false specialization; no additional field is
added to every Lua frame or register view. Actual inactive-path performance is
still measured, not assumed unchanged from that source structure.

The reference Lua VM likewise distinguishes a resumed hooked instruction from
a new hook delivery; see [Lua's trace-execution implementation](https://www.lua.org/source/5.4/ldebug.c.html#luaG_traceexec).
This is not a claim that all existing global-hook ownership or combined-event
semantics are now equivalent to Lua's implementation.

#### Register-view base redundancy — measured and withdrawn

All three `LuaRegisters` constructors set `base` to the length of `upper_stack`:
the physical and projection constructors use `split_at_mut(base)`, while the
test-only detached constructor uses an empty upper slice and zero base.
The private view therefore stores the same boundary twice. The next isolated
trial removes only that duplicate word, deriving capture, close-list and JIT
projection boundaries from the existing upper slice. Physical `Frame::Lua`
bases remain unchanged; no stack pointer/value survives a callback or reborrow.
The scoped raw-pointer accessor must read only its already-permitted upper-stack
field, never borrow the current-frame values while field loans exist.

This differs from the rejected register-view constructor inlining and frame
tuple/accessor trials. It adds no inline hint, cache, mode split or accounting
change. The hypothesized benefit is less frame-view materialization and fewer
redundant boundary loads, not a measured speedup. Freeze current production
and no-feature controls, verify split/close/capture semantics and footprint,
then compare exact-image profiles and both native/feature-cost timing gates.

The trial removed the duplicate word. Dedicated native tests verified **64-byte
no-feature / 80-byte JIT views on x86-64**, every split boundary from zero through
the complete stack, capture read/write hook coordinates, capture reuse and
closing, close-list order, and unchanged PC/fuel. Focused verification passes
**83 executions / 15 summaries**, with formatting and all-feature checking.
The first fixture compile failed because `Value` deliberately has no `PartialEq`;
the corrected fixture matches exact integer variants rather than changing
runtime equality. That failed log is retained separately.

#### Preferred call-resumption dispatcher — test-only prototype

`84beab8` adds a source selector for one reachable fixed-arity Call enclosed by
a numeric-loop backedge, with a native post-call operation. It refuses ambiguous,
variable, unreachable, non-native and non-enclosing cases without adding storage.
This is a source-shape heuristic, not evidence that the selected PC is hot.

The test-only CLIF prototype keeps the original full-width entry bounds check,
all operation trampolines and budget headers. Inside the valid-PC dispatcher it
adds an equality guard leading directly to the selected existing trampoline;
the original jump-table instruction moves to the false branch. No PC is removed,
no body is entered past its budget guard, and no value or lease survives a new
callback boundary. Cranelift verification and an independent restoration check
compare the remaining original function after removing only the added routing.
Wrong selected PC, inverted comparison, budget bypass and altered budget checks
are explicitly refused; invalid preferred indices leave the function unchanged.

execution, bounded compiler-resource integration and paired profiling/timing

companions are explicitly reused and reverified, not called fresh captures.

**127,768,425** instructions versus the prior **124,777,527**. Three fresh
processes with the same candidate image instead execute **123,737,277 /
123,737,277 / 123,737,196**. Three fresh processes with the unchanged prior image
each execute **123,997,452**. All complete result/resource/counter records match;
the image hashes remain unchanged. The prior image's 780,156-instruction VM
difference is therefore not stable and cannot be attributed to fallback
outlining alone.

An independent raw-PC audit explains the candidate's table-probe variation:

| Same candidate image | Key identity checks | Content fallback calls | Successful value loads |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Initial process | 129,672 | 64,836 | 64,836 |
| Each of three fresh processes | 64,836 | 0 | 64,836 |

The initial process checks an extra rejected key for each successful native
lookup. These are real costs in the process-seeded hash table, not extra Lua
operations. Longer sampling inside one process does not resample that table
layout. Keep all observations and add independent process repetitions; do not
disable hashing randomness or waive existing gates. VM metadata lookups also
use a map, but this audit does not prove the cause of their variation.

register/stack placement. No hardware speedup or elapsed regression is inferred
from that diagnostic. No elapsed timing was run for this placement.

non-inlined content fallback. It passes its own **43 focused and ten Rust-only

This removes the first placement's observed successful-path instruction cost;
no high-probe process was observed in these profiles, so a negative-probe saving
is not measured. Changed simulated branch misses are not hardware evidence.

Three native timing campaigns finish **13,608 measured executions** with zero
counter/resource mismatches. Ten of twelve callback control/candidate ratios
are below one; ten of twelve candidate callback gates and four metamethod gates

iterations / 216 audited gate reports** finish, with candidate failures **21/72**

Both runtime placements are withdrawn; the independent collision fixture stays.

The cold variant did not run its own full Force suite; the first placement's

`c7d10b3` gives generic payload writes an explicit descriptor contract. Checked
descriptors retain all pointer checks. FrameBound writes rely on their bound
scalar-pointer invariant, removing five IR instructions per generic write while
retaining tag equality, Boolean bits <= 1, bit-preserving float conversion,
byte-width Boolean stores and the existing helper/copy/terminal paths. Both
exact expansion checks account for the reduction; conservative admission limits
are unchanged. The emitted verifier rejects contract substitution and checks the
complete contract-specific instruction shape.

#### Numeric-union read proofs — callback and upvalue gaps reduced

`d58e38b` makes numeric reads ask for a distinct `Tag::Numeric` fact rather than trying
exact INTEGER and NUMBER facts separately. The bounded search accepts the
verified I64 predicate `(tag & -2) == 2`, either operand order, and incoming
paths that independently establish INTEGER or NUMBER. It still requires fresh
loads from the exact queried register, valid guards on every incoming path,
independent emitted verification and the existing depth/work budgets. Calls and
unrecognized stores invalidate the proof. Writes explicitly ask for
`Tag::Exact`; an ambiguous numeric guard cannot authorize a same-tag store.
No runtime contract, production transport selector or Off default changes.

#### Per-field alias regions — no useful workload gain; resumption limit demonstrated

`b446e86` tests a finer classification than the universal-region trial: every
eight-byte scratch tag/payload field has its own region, and the three exit
stores share an exit region. This remains test-only
`Failure::RequireFieldMemory`, with ordinary transport, integer-loop augmentation
and prepared-key helpers preserved. No shipping selection changes.

The classifier admits only eight-byte I64/F64 loads/stores at aligned offsets
inside the verified register prefix, or the exact exit stores at offsets 0/8/12.
All other memory roots, overlapping/partial accesses, global-value loads,
preexisting regions and oversized source flag tables are refused. Equal scratch
and exit IR roots are refused. Scratch fields are disjoint intervals in the
same initialized array; `abi::invoke` supplies a separate newly created Exit.
There are no admitted direct host-memory accesses. Opaque calls invalidate all
regions in the pinned compiler. Entry-to-entry inlining is not performed after
this pass; introducing it would require revisiting region identity/relocation.

The normalized emitted checker requires full source-function equality after
restoring flag handles/tables, and independently checks region selection for
each original access. Publication is atomic. Verification records are fallible;
table admission reserves 16 KiB plus 384 bytes per memory access through
compiler/module destruction. This remains bounded additional-table accounting,
**not** complete accounting for the function clone or optimizer workspace.
The extra reservation is observable: integer snapshot peak rises from 9,147 to
48,099 bytes, and callbacks from 10,737 to 41,253 bytes in the profile image.

`cc1e408` adds a causal compiler diagnostic. In the same native fixture,
per-field regions reduce optimized loads from **4 to 3** with one entry, while
adding a second resumption edge leaves **4 loads with either selection**.
Both entry PCs execute with correct helper mutations, floating payload bits and
exit records. The metadata is therefore being used, not ignored. The actual
ordinary entry dispatcher exposes a trampoline for each opcode
(`entry_flow::Paths::emit_entry`), so earlier stores generally cannot dominate
later resumable bodies. The diagnostic demonstrates this constraint; it does
not establish that it explains every measured runtime cost. Do not remove valid
resumption/fuel entries to manufacture a speedup.

#### Universal alias-region experiment — measured, no useful gain

`1b98403` implements the previously proposed single-region experiment on the
ordinary scratch transport. It is selected only by test-only
`Failure::RequireUniversalMemory`; production lowering and the Off default are
unchanged. Integer-loop augmentation and prepared-key helpers remain enabled.

The pass runs after the existing source checks and lowering. It assigns one
region to actual memory instructions, retaining every other memory flag. It
makes no claim that two buffers or registers cannot overlap. The emitted checker
normalizes the changed flag handles/tables and requires full `Function` equality
with the verified source, including control flow, signatures and other metadata.
The source is replaced only after verification succeeds. Calls remain fences in
the pinned Cranelift implementation; trap/alignment/readonly/endian flags remain
unchanged. Native tests execute both overlapping and separate input addresses,
including a helper that mutates memory between loads.

An initial integration failure exposed an important API detail:
`InstructionData::memflags()` also returns flags for `bitcast`, which uses the
`LoadNoOffset` instruction format but is not a memory operation. Annotating it
fails Cranelift verification. Selection now checks `can_load`/`can_store`, retains
the original flag table and includes integer/float bitcast round trips in the
native fixture. Global-value loads and unflagged non-call loads are refused
rather than left outside the access classification.

The pass admits at most 32 source flag entries, reserves 16 KiB for bounded
additional flag/region tables through compiler destruction, and uses fallible
ledger-backed verification records. Tests cover exact quota boundaries,
oversized tables, malformed/uncovered reads, repeated application and atomic
refusal. This is **not** complete compiler accounting: the cloned function and
other Cranelift transient allocations remain within the previously documented
unaccounted compiler-workspace scope. No resource or release gate is closed.

| Allocation/GC | 3,612,099 / 3,612,040 | 3,609,316 / 3,609,311 |

Mapped code sizes match in every pair. Numeric and callback counts are exactly

The next alias-analysis investigation should distinguish proven nonoverlapping
scratch fields, not merely rename all memory with one region. Ordinary lowering
uses eight-byte tag/payload accesses at checked offsets from the same scratch
base; a store to a tag currently advances the same memory version as payload
stores. A per-field experiment still needs complete address/range classification,
proof that exit/host accesses cannot overlap those fields, call invalidation,
stable region identities, bounded compiler storage and the same workload gates.

and all elapsed-time/platform/resource/release acceptance gates remain open.

#### Classifier and address costs — measured reductions, rollout still withheld

Three incremental changes continue the integrated transport experiment:

  to 11,890,273; the corresponding ordinary control remains 10,754,709.
- `b57ae97` separates tag classification from scalar layout measurement.
  Boolean/integer/number offsets are measured from Rust-constructed values once
  per header, rather than recalculated for each register or helper write.
  The classifier only writes a byte tag. Callback instructions fall to
  11,230,077. A new test compares the measured layout against actual live scalar
  field addresses across widths 1/7/16/64/256, preserving bit-exact reads.
- `a79b185` specializes generated addresses when those three measured offsets
  agree. The compiler emits one measured displacement instead of a runtime
  offset-table lookup. It does not assume a numeric offset or an enum tag layout.
  The generic table-based lowering remains available for nonuniform layouts.
  Its checker verifies the measured offset and every emitted address/guard;
  mutation tests cover both paths. Each specialized pointer rewrite adds 11
  instructions rather than 16; admission retains the conservative existing bound.

#### Typed strided VM transport — integrated candidate, not a shipping selection

`59fbb1b`, `70737fa` and `f5e7490` move the experiment beyond the one-field
lookup probe. A test-selected `RequireStrided` entry now compiles real Lua
snapshots, owns its generated code through the existing cache/lease machinery,
and executes through the real VM's canonical-frame path. The ordinary shipping
transport and Off default are unchanged.

The frame header contains one canonical allocation base, measured per-kind
payload offsets and byte tags for the register prefix. Boolean, integer and
number fields remain in the public `Vec<Value>`; nil and reference descriptors
have null field pointers. Native writes touch only existing scalar fields.
Type-changing writes and reference copies materialize through Rust, rather than
writing private enum discriminants. Helper boundaries retire the old base before
canonical reborrows and renew its provenance afterwards. Prepared helpers use
the same verified packed operands and full hash as the ordinary compiler.

The backend first applies the existing source/effect-verified FrameBound
lowering, then replaces descriptor loads with checked header-address patterns.
The second pass preserves SSA results, independently checks emitted addresses,
tag bounds, widths, memory flags and null selection, and charges its rewrite
records and instruction expansion. Mutation tests reject altered patterns;
quota failures preserve the original IR and release temporary records.

The initial integration passes all seven frozen workloads with identical results
and all 25 compared execution counters. It also passes 24 script families across

bound. The strided preflight now charges the additional 17 instructions per nil

#### Prepared strided lookups — helper-inclusive savings, no runtime selection

`a83abd5` shares `Frame::prehashed_up_table` through the existing `Transport`
trait, rather than duplicating lookup semantics or replacing the prepared lookup
with a generic key lookup. Test-only direct/strided adapters preserve the packed
operand word, both halves of the process-seeded hash and the full 32-bit PC.
`d020e9b` adds independent expected-value/control assertions to the differential.

Rust and generated controllers each pass **288 comparisons**: eight value forms,
twelve scenarios and three PCs. Cases include open aliases, reserved operand
bits, invalid constant/upvalue/destination indices, borrowed-table panics,
initially noninteger admission and a perturbed hash. Hash perturbation checks
lookup parity, not a new runtime hash-rejection guarantee; source verification
still supplies valid prepared hashes. Both controllers preserve canonical values,
all helper counters, fuel, PC, panic state and the separate readiness result.
The first run caught a packed-control bug: an initially retired header was not
restored after the helper produced an integer. The corrected control and failed
debug/Miri attempts are retained; this was not a production runtime bug.

Eight immutable software profiles compare full packing/writeback plus the actual
`PREHASHED_ENTRY` against scoped admission plus the shared prepared canonical
helper. Each runs 100,000 generated arithmetic/lookup transitions. The callback
shape derives its width and operands from the frozen `rust_callbacks` source,
but does **not** execute the whole script or call the returned callback; the
probe explicitly asserts zero callback invocations. It admits only the one
integer field used by this component's arithmetic, not a whole-function mask.

| Component | Packed instructions | Strided instructions | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Single-slot scalar lookup | 39,200,026 | 38,200,028 | -2.551% |
| Seven-slot callback lookup | 55,500,020 | 41,700,028 | -24.865% |

Both repeats reproduce these instruction totals and validate every result,
helper counter, PC and fuel value. These are helper-inclusive component savings,
not elapsed-time measurements or a production callback speedup. Their images are

#### Strided helper transitions — actual helpers verified, VM integration open

`f4d51bd` extends the strided experiment across Luna's ten generic helper
operations. A scoped session owns access to `helpers::Frame`; its mutable header
is separate from the original immutable arithmetic window. The adapter retires
the header before borrowing the canonical frame for a helper, then admits the
current fields again after completion. Declines and caught panics stop that
session, and re-entry returns the terminal status without repeating effects or
incrementing counters. A completed helper that creates a noninteger value is
still reported as completed, with subsequent integer access disabled separately.

A real Cranelift controller performs integer arithmetic before and after the
helper call, reloads the current header after the call, and skips the suffix when
admission fails. Its Rust counterpart exercises the same boundary under Miri.
The existing proxy-helper oracle now compares **10 helpers x 10 scenarios** for
each controller. It checks canonical values/reference identities, table effects,
open/closed upvalues, all eight helper counters, PC, fuel, declines and caught
panics. The table oracle also checks key3, which the arithmetic prefix can affect
through `SetList`. Additional tests cover all value kinds, integer restoration
within one session, terminal re-entry and preexisting panics.

Debug strided10/helper6/ABI10/native18/heap20 tests and no/all-feature checks pass.
Final Miri checks pass under Stacked (helper4 seed81, complete model7 seed83) and
Tree Borrows (helper4 plus complete model7, seed82). Generated execution is
checked natively, not claimed under Miri. The frozen optimized image passes
strided10 and helper6. Native Memcheck passes helper6 with zero reported errors,
zero definitely/indirectly lost bytes, 48 possibly lost bytes and 632 reachable
bytes. The residual allocations are retained in the report, not described as
zero-allocation acceptance. Binary/source identities are checked before both
optimized and Memcheck execution.

This is not yet a backend mode, source/effect verifier or VM dispatch change.
The existing helpers decline metamethod cases rather than invoke user callbacks,
so this does not prove actual callback re-entry or stack relocation. The hot
prepared-key `GetUpTable` entry is separate from generic `call_direct` and is not
covered by this adapter; its seeded hash/packed operand contract must be retained.
Projection, code-lease/resource accounting and full PC/fuel/native-coverage
integration remain open. No helper-inclusive performance gain, production fix,
hardware timing or release acceptance is claimed.

#### Strided integer-field transport — scoped model, not runtime acceptance

`8bab591` adds a test-only alternative to per-register payload descriptors: a
three-word header containing an integer-field base, the Rust `Value` stride and
the current frame length. Admission matches the required current values as
`Integer`, measures their payload offsets through Rust references, checks offset
agreement and derives the final raw pointer from the whole mutable slice. It
does not assume a private enum discriminant or payload offset, change the public
`Vec<Value>` stack, cache values across host mutations, or write reference fields
or enum tags. A noncopyable invocation window borrows both frame and code owner.

Six focused tests pass, including an independently generated Cranelift entry
running the same edge/seeded wrapping and preservation corpus as the Rust entry.
Coverage includes same-index writes, first/last slots, frame width boundaries,
all value kinds, current-value rebinding, unchanged neighboring references,
scope unwinding and null/short headers. Four Rust-only tests also pass Miri
Stacked Borrows seed74 and Tree Borrows seed75. Generated code is tested natively,
not under Miri. Existing ABI10/native18/heap20 regressions and formatting pass.
An initial `MemFlags` API mismatch was fixed to `MemFlagsData`; the failed build
is retained separately from passing runs.

This is not integrated into the VM or source/effect verifier. It cannot cover
type-changing destinations, callbacks, helper reborrows or stack relocation
without explicit retirement and fresh admission. It has no compiler/resource
quota integration and does not establish a GC-lifecycle or release gate. Existing
numeric kernels and production scratch transport remain unchanged.

`make jit-strided-profile-build jit-strided-profile-run` compares this binding
against full `Slot::from_value` packing and `write_back`, using the same generated
integer-add entry and 100,000 calls per shape. Seven shapes include a single slot,
mixed frames with two admitted fields, and dense admission at widths 7/16/256.
The dense cases deliberately measure conservative admission of unused integer
fields; they are not full dense arithmetic workloads. Collection excludes JIT
construction and checks every resulting value and reference identity. Frozen
binary/source hashes and positive execution checks accompany each software
profile. These are synthetic transport costs, not callback execution, hardware
timing, full-runtime speedups or acceptance.

The first fourteen profiles show mixed-frame savings but dense-admission
regressions. Disassembly identifies unnecessary checked reconstruction of each
containing value's address. `fdd4386` measures the offset directly between the
matched value reference and its payload reference instead. All admission checks
remain; whole-slice provenance still supplies the final mutable pointer. Its
six focused tests and four Miri tests under each borrowing model pass. Another
fourteen profiles preserve identical packed-control instruction totals and
validated results while removing the dense-frame instruction regression.
The one-slot case remains adverse; none of this justifies unconditional selection.

are **61.885% and 39.738%** respectively; single-slot binding still costs
**26.154% more**. Both Miri models pass again (seeds 78/79), and native Memcheck
reports the same zero-error/residual-allocation result. Final fmt/focused6/ABI10/
native18/heap20 and no/all-feature checks pass.

instead of the frozen control's `strip=false`; its identity check correctly

`73b609225834a42f9a2501be785a4f3fdd33d4e10dbf29eab15c3b03eef6090c`.
No source activation was made. There is no production performance improvement

#### Borrowed scalar matching: runtime forms rejected, models retained

`ad96fcb` retains two test-only import models and an 8,206-value differential.
Both match a borrowed `Value` directly; the second keeps numeric values inline
and outlines nonnumeric matching. This differs from the older borrowed-iterator
trial, which still copied each value into `Slot::from_value`. Neither model
changes value layout, tags, reference rooting, register coverage or public APIs.

Three temporary runtime variants replaced ordinary scratch imports: direct
borrowed matching, forced inlining of that match, and numeric-first matching
with a cold remainder. The first and third passed ABI10/native18/heap20/
upvalue7 tests and compilation checks; the annotation-only refinement reran
ABI10/heap20. Twelve immutable full-runtime profiles compare all three
variants with one control across callbacks, metamethods and upvalues. All
eighteen smoke records and complete profile execution/resource records match.

Callback instructions increase from **126,201,876** to **127,368,798** for
both direct/forced-inline forms (+0.9246%), and **127,629,922** for the cold
remainder (+1.1316%). The direct match increases seven-register wrapper self
instructions from 20,233,235 to 21,400,157. Disassembly has fourteen static
indirect jumps instead of seven; collected indirect branches increase by
453,943, exactly seven per native entry. These are jump-table branches, not
seven new function calls. Forced inlining leaves callback instruction totals
unchanged. The numeric/cold refinement also raises metamethod instructions
2.8344%; its lower upvalue instruction count does not fix the target regression.
These are software profiles, not hardware timing or a claim about elapsed costs.

No hardware campaign was run for these candidates. All production hooks and
annotations are withdrawn; only the model/oracle and Make targets remain.
The oracle covers every Value kind, integer extremes, signed zero, infinities,
generated integer/float payloads and mutation between imports. Both final models
pass Stacked Borrows seed72 and Tree Borrows seed73 under `nix develop .#miri`,
one test each with 38 existing warnings. The default dev shell and separately
installed dated rustup toolchain lacked Miri; both failed launch logs remain.

Restored formatting, the focused oracle, ABI10/native18/heap20 and no-feature/
all-feature checks pass. The rebuilt default executable is byte-identical to
the frozen control, SHA256
`73b609225834a42f9a2501be785a4f3fdd33d4e10dbf29eab15c3b03eef6090c`;
all eighteen fresh non-timing smoke records match. Evidence is under
`target/jit-evidence/short-slice-performance/reference-match/`, including all
three patches/images, twelve profiles, disassembly and `audit.json`.
`make jit-reference-import` and `make jit-reference-import-miri` rerun the
retained oracle. Full performance/platform/resource/release acceptance remains
open; do not retry borrowed matching or numeric-first import source rewrites
without evidence of a different generated import sequence.

#### Wide prepared-helper ABI: compiler validated, runtime trial withdrawn

`cc5397f` and `be37d28` probe a four-argument GetUpTable entry: host, scratch,
packed operands plus the full 32-bit PC in one u64, and the seeded hash in
another u64. Public values, stack storage, source admission, production helper
signatures and native selection remain unchanged. The direct entry expands
the existing helper macro body, retaining lookup, projection, panic capture,
PC-before-effects, counters and panic materialization rather than bypassing them.

The first adapter merely converts back to the six-argument Rust entry. Its
100,000-call generated probe costs 26,300,023 versus 26,100,023 instructions,
despite reducing the native stub from 39 to 35 bytes. That adapter is not an
optimization. The direct-body model removes the extra conversion call.

Two complete direct-body profile sets reproduce identical instruction totals:
scalar lookup 28,900,023 to 28,100,023; callback-shaped lookup 28,300,023 to
27,500,023. Both save eight instructions per helper invocation, about 2.77%
and 2.83% respectively. The callback shape imports the frozen workload's real
source and derives its seven-register width, packed operands 327683 and source
PC 5, returning the current callback reference. It does not execute the callback
or the benchmark loop. Native stubs shrink 44 to 42 bytes for this shape.
These are component instruction profiles, not whole-runtime speedups or hardware
acceptance. Cross-build scalar totals are not comparable because helper outlining
changes in the test artifact. Four of the eight saved instructions are an old
entry shim in this artifact; production inlining may change that benefit.

The encoding model checks 81 full-PC/reserved-bit combinations. Actual generated
calls match the six-argument entry in 35 value/missing/metamethod/borrow-panic/null
host cases across five PCs through u32::MAX. The existing helper differential now
compares generic, prepared, wide-adapter and wide-direct entries. GNU passes
29 helper tests, 20 heap integration tests and the four-way differential; the
profile-only test remains explicitly ignored outside profiling. Stacked seed 0
and Tree seed 1 each report 28+1+1 model passes, with existing warnings and no
generated-code execution under Miri. No-feature/all-feature checks and formatting
pass. Profile audits verify counters, source operands, exact native byte sizes,
positive collection, source/image hashes and one executed test per capture.

The shared macro refactor's actual production benchmark is rebuilt, still using
the six-argument ABI. Its fresh nine-case smoke matches all eighteen non-timing
records, and callback instruction profiles match exactly at 126,201,795. Neither
check establishes elapsed-time or release acceptance.

`85cfb9f` adds a test-only four-argument compiler selection. The independent
helper-flow verifier checks its signature, both u64 constants, source PC,
operands and hash; the extra signature workspace is charged. Ordinary helper
imports retain six arguments, including writes in mixed read/write sources.
Production selection and its generic/projected/resource fallback are unchanged.

`make jit-wide-compiler` passes three new compiler tests and nine existing
prepared-key tests. Native wide/ordinary execution matches in 1,155 paired
cases over four sources, every source entry plus invalid entries, five budgets
and seven value/decline/borrow-panic states. The comparison includes exits,
charged instructions, frame PC, helper counters, captured panic state, scratch,
canonical registers and global effects; 205 successful reads execute in each
variant. All twenty injected call-flow corruptions are refused before
installation. Exact-workspace-limit and one-byte-below checks release snapshot
charges and executable mappings; unsupported register-key sources refuse the
experimental selection. These are compiler-path tests, not full-runtime speedups.

The subsequent runtime trial below does not justify production activation.
Evidence: `target/jit-evidence/short-slice-performance/wide-helper-*`.
Compiler evidence: `target/jit-evidence/short-slice-performance/wide-compiler-*`.

The full baseline `make jit-test jit-heap check check-all` passed, including
1,325 library tests with ten explicitly ignored tests and the integration
suite. A fresh opt-level-3, unstripped control was frozen at `e36cd80` before
temporarily enabling the compiler path. Native18, heap20, upvalue7 and
resource28+3+3+14 tests passed for that activation. Each subsequent inlining

All four profiles confirm execution of `helpers::wide::direct`. Default

#### Guarded built-in call fusion: hardware tradeoff rejected

An exact-instance `setmetatable` fast path replaces the ordinary callback
transition only for fixed two-argument plain-table operations. The registry
holds a weak identity, not a global-name or function-address assumption.
Protected, weak/finalizing, borrowed or invalid tables, active hooks,
interruption, insufficient boundary fuel, frame limits and relevant open
captures/close slots retain the ordinary path. Normal and tail calls use the
original fuel charges; transitions remain interpreted instructions in coverage.

The first GNU step oracle passes 196 paired schedules with collection between
steps and 70 actual fused calls. In the metamethod case at budget 4096, 22 calls
fuse: the two initializations and all twenty loop tail calls. The retained
tail-only variant still passes all 196 schedules, with 49 fused calls overall
and twenty in that metamethod case. The trace now also compares pending Lua
return state. Separate fixtures cover 96 admission states, fifteen root/normal/
multiple/variable/metamethod tail-return states, scope unwind and weak identity
survival, collection and replacement. No-feature/all-feature checks pass.

A persistent instruction hook with zero fuel fails to complete even in the
ordinary control. It remains covered by a 64-step bounded trace comparison;
the completion matrix separately uses a self-clearing hook. No completion
claim is made for the persistent-hook case. The final three primitive and two
identity tests pass both Stacked Borrows (seed 0) and Tree Borrows (seed 1)
Miri, with existing warnings; no native execution is claimed from Miri.

Three experimental production binaries were measured, each after the paired
step tests and eighteen native integration tests passed:

| Variant | Metamethod CPU instructions | Callback CPU instructions |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Normal and tail calls | -4.430% | +0.103% |
| Tail calls only, VM-side check | -4.789% | +0.156% |
| Tail calls only, outlined transition | -4.351% | unchanged |

These are Callgrind instruction counts, not speedups. The outlined variant
measures 78,314,650 to 74,906,944 metamethod instructions and exactly
126,201,876 callback instructions in both images. All non-timing records match.

Five complete hardware screens ran 120 commands and 2,160 timing-summary rows:
two for normal/tail fusion, one for VM-side tail fusion and two for the outlined
transition. Every screen uses four rotated control/candidate/same-image-placebo
windows on CPUs 0 and 16, unchanged paired eleven-sample workloads and gates,

The production hook is withdrawn. Only the test-only tail transition and its

#### Branched integer-loop direction: hardware trial rejected

The callback kernel computes both signed integer-limit comparisons before
selecting one according to step direction. A new test-only rewrite moves each
comparison into its selected branch. It runs after ordinary source/entry/exit
verification and retains the original comparisons, overflow handling, values,
budgets and native instruction accounting. Shared comparison results, including
successor arguments, are refused; there are fixed function-size/site caps.
This is not the earlier combined numeric-tag guard experiment.

The GNU native oracle covers 231,525 index/limit/step, PC and budget combinations
against both the unchanged kernel and the scalar model. Candidate and control
slots match bitwise; model NaN results are compared as NaNs. Bounds include
signed integer overflow, negative/zero steps, mixed floats, infinities, invalid
scalar kinds, zero budgets and unknown entry PCs. Pure IR tests check idempotence
and refusal without mutation. These are prototype checks, not production
activation or full performance acceptance.

`make jit-disassembly` now imports the frozen callback workload and emits both
ordinary and experimental kernels, including the prepared-helper address.
Both initial x86-64 kernels occupy 2,160 bytes. Assembly confirms an actual
direction branch replaces the integer conditional selection. The diagnostic
invokes only the helper-free prefix, stopping at GetUpTable without a host;
it does not claim to execute callbacks.

The experimental production build then ran the unchanged real workloads.
Two callback profiles collected 126,201,795 / 126,201,876 control instructions
versus 126,137,027 for the candidate: only about 0.051% fewer overall. The
metamethod profile instead increased from 78,328,922 to 78,446,840. All full
non-timing records matched. Callgrind branch-miss estimates are not hardware
branch-predictor measurements, and instrumented durations are not speedups.
The first candidate build accidentally retained release stripping, producing
zero collection at the named Executor boundary; the Make guard rejected it.
Its failed log remains separate from six valid symbol-preserving captures.

Two complete speed-profile screens ran 48 commands, with 864 timing-summary
rows and 432 unchanged workload gates. Each screen used four rotated
control/candidate/same-image-placebo windows on CPUs 0 and 16, eleven paired
samples per workload, immutable binaries, identical hardlink launch paths,
source/image hashes and contention telemetry. CPU order was reversed for the
second screen. No owned build, test or profiler overlapped hardware timing.
All non-timing fields matched in both screens, including native coverage,
helper work and memory counters.

| Control/candidate Auto time ratio | CPU 0 first / repeat | CPU 16 first / repeat |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Rust callbacks | 1.1275 / 0.9890 | 0.9889 / 0.9987 |
| Metamethods | 1.0993 / 0.9713 | 0.9870 / 0.9959 |
| Array tables | 0.8996 / 0.9672 | 0.9549 / 0.9894 |

The first CPU-0 callback gain did not reproduce. Callback gates failed 6/8
and 7/8; metamethod gates failed 3/8 in each screen. Aggregate acceptance

from 0.8546 / 0.9082 initially to 0.9976 / 0.9632 on repeat. These mixed
results do not establish a hardware cause or justify activation.

The production hook was removed; only the test-only rewrite, boundary corpus

#### Arithmetic entry precheck: rejected at profiling

A fresh canonical operand check was tested before ordinary native scratch
packing. It declined only Add/Sub/Mul/Div entries with a nonnumeric operand,
without changing PC, values, fuel or statistics. Numeric strings still fell
back to the interpreter; each invocation reread current operands rather than
caching a failed type. No skipped attempt was recorded as a native invocation.

Three candidate tests passed, including direct generated-code guard checks and
table-to-number-to-table mutation across repeated runtime entries. Another 71
test executions passed across native execution, numeric exits, errors,
suspension and helper targets. Formatting and compilation checks passed.

The actual metamethod workload disproved the proposed benefit. Fresh paired
Callgrind profiles of the frozen integrated control and candidate both report
25,751 native entries, 12,801 guard exits, 116,239 native bytecodes and 1,021
interpreted bytecodes. Every non-timing benchmark field matches. Collected CPU
instructions increase from 78,318,230 to 78,714,091 (0.5055%). Aggregate guard
counts therefore did not establish avoidable zero-work arithmetic entries;
the implemented check removes none in this workload. Profiled wall times are
not hardware performance evidence, and no hardware campaign was started for
this ineffective candidate.

The production check and opcode accessor were removed. Only a generated-code
regression test remains: 147,456 invocations cover four arithmetic operators,
register/constant operands, destination aliases, reference and scalar values,
numeric strings, NaN/infinities, signed zero and zero-budget priority. It checks
that failed entry guards preserve all scratch slots and execute no bytecodes.
Run it with `make jit-entry-guard`.

musl target reused an older test binary and initially reported success with
zero matching tests; that run is not validation. The Make target now requires
the named test in the harness listing before execution. It rejects that stale
binary with exit 2 and accepts both current binaries. No claim is made about
the cause of Cargo's stale reuse.

Candidate source patch, binary/hash, profiles, independent non-timing audit
and validation logs are retained under
`target/jit-evidence/short-slice-performance/entry-guard-*`. This is a rejected
optimization, not a runtime regression fix or progress on performance gates.

#### Prepared register-table keys: measured and rejected

An ordinary-transport trial extends prepared string hashes from `GetUpTable`
to eligible constant-string `GetTable` operations, without storing GC addresses
or changing table equality, current-value reads, weak handling or metamethod
declines. Register/non-string table keys retain ordinary lookup; their presence
does not disable existing eligible upvalue-table preparation. Hash storage stays
optional, charged and released before the existing resource-limited retry.

Twelve focused tests pass, including register-source/destination aliasing,
non-table receivers, borrowed-table panics, source eligibility, real native
mutation/GC reads and forty malformed-helper-flow variants. Twenty public heap
tests pass. The first broad boundary run passes 1,209 tests but fails one
resource fixture: `peak - 1` admits ordinary compilation after optional hashes

#### Prepared string-key lookups — incremental improvement integrated

Commits `48d5928`, `69480f5`, `cfef771` and `4f83fa4` were developed and tested
on `experiment/prepared-string-keys`, then fast-forwarded into this branch.
Ordinary native `GetUpTable` operations with constant string keys embed the
existing process-seeded hash. Every read still checks full key equality and
current table/weak-value state. Register-key functions and other entry modes
retain the original helper. The six-argument ABI packs three original byte
operands into one word and carries the hash in two words; PC remains unchanged.
No GC address is cached, no reference descriptor gains pointer bits, and no
Value/String/raw-stack layout or public contract changes.

Optional snapshot hashes cover only the required prefix, at most 256 entries.
On resource refusal compilation releases them and retries ordinary lowering
before the existing eviction policy; failure-injection modes do not retry.
An exact-workspace-limit test demonstrates prepared refusal followed by ordinary
success, with storage released. Generic C entries and the prepared Rust entry
share one macro body for panic handling, PC, projection and writeback.

The final source passes **1,824 GNU Auto executions / 88 summaries**, eight
ignored diagnostics, plus nine focused GNU and nine focused musl executions.
The latter covers all twenty helper-flow corruptions, exact resource fallback,
borrow-conflict panic equivalence, actual native reads, and distinct cached keys
through value mutation and GC. Three table tests pass on musl, with one ignored
diagnostic. Stacked seed 76 and Tree seed 77 each pass five pure tests. Native
Memcheck passes nine tests with zero errors and zero definite/indirect leaks;
48 possible TLS bytes and 632 reachable bytes remain. These are targeted checks,
not new ARM64/i686 or full release acceptance.

Fresh final software profiles reduce callback instructions **5.953% shipping /
4.560% speed**; allocation/GC instructions equal baseline. All thirteen event
totals equal independently summed self-costs and all execution counters match.
Callback snapshot peak grows **10,705 → 10,737 bytes**; code/retained metadata do
not grow in this workload. Fewer instructions alone were insufficient: the
intermediate direct-only entry regressed CPU0 speed callbacks in every window,
and forcing a shared wrapper inline added allocation work. Both were rejected.

Four fixed final timing campaigns retain **192 commands / 3,456 case rows /
1,728 paired gates**, CPUs 0/16, four rotated windows per campaign, eleven paired
samples and an identical-control placebo. No owned build/test/profile overlapped

**1.12238 / 1.05719** on CPU16 (shipping/speed); 63 of 64 candidate comparisons
improve. Placebo medians are 0.99971/1.00456 and 1.00024/0.99584 respectively.

Collateral results remain mixed: CPU16 speed arrays have a 0.98014 raw median

Median control/candidate Auto ratios for callbacks are **0.98075 / 0.96383** on
