#### Scheduled input imports — boundary model, not a runtime fix

`91ba2df` adds a test-only native boundary model and reproducible Make targets:
`jit-import-model`, `jit-import-model-miri`, `jit-import-profile-build` and
`jit-import-profile-run`. The model compares full seven-slot packing, individual
checked importer calls, and one statically specialized bulk importer. Bulk
imports initialize all slots; omitted inputs are canonical proxies, not cached
values. Generated code checks import refusal before accessing scratch storage.

GNU and fresh-target musl each pass three tests with one ignored diagnostic.
Stacked seed 65 and Tree seed 66 each pass two pure tests. The native differential
test compiles both import variants for every seven-bit mask, refreshes mutated
inputs and exercises refusal with uninitialized scratch. Memcheck passes this
test with zero errors and zero definite/indirect leaks; 48 possible TLS bytes and
544 reachable bytes remain. This is not a whole-runtime memory validation.

The refined model uses production-shaped full packing and six integer inputs
plus nil. **24 profiles** each execute 100,000 verified entries; independent
analysis checks all thirteen event totals against summed self-costs. Model
source and binary checks pass. Initial mixed-value profiles are kept separately
and are not pooled with these results.

| Instructions per 100,000 entries | Shipping | Speed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Five inputs used, full packing | 13,800,022 | 11,300,023 |
| Five inputs used, individual imports | 21,800,022 | 19,500,023 |
| Five inputs used, bulk import | 11,100,022 | 10,900,023 |
| Seven inputs used, full packing | 14,400,022 | 11,900,023 |
| Seven inputs used, bulk import | 15,000,022 | 15,000,023 |

At five inputs, bulk saves **27 / 4 instructions per entry**, or approximately
**19.6% / 3.5% of this boundary model**, while increasing data reads and writes.
At seven inputs it loses **6 / 31 instructions per entry**. Individual checked
calls lose at five and seven inputs. These are software instruction counts,
not application speedups or evidence that the callback regression is fixed.

Production import code is unchanged by this probe. A safe Rust static-mask packer
can test whether compile-time specialization avoids the earlier dynamic-mask
loop overhead without adding a native helper ABI. It still needs source-derived
read-before-definition proofs, charged optional metadata, exact native coverage,
alias/PC/budget/GC/borrow tests, and original end-to-end acceptance gates. Full
packing must remain available for ineligible or unprofitable entries. Evidence:
`target/jit-evidence/short-slice-performance/scheduled-import-final/`.

#### Precomputed string-key hashes — measured lookup model only

`d87fc1c` adds a test-only, GC-free `PreparedHash(u64)` model and Make targets.
Queries still inspect the current table, compare complete keys and upgrade weak
values on every read. Three tests cover distinct equal string allocations,
binary/long keys, missing/false/NaN values, growth, mutation, deletion,
reinsertion, clearing, forced hash collisions and collection in all weak modes.
GNU and fresh-target musl each pass all three tests. Stacked seed 61 and Tree
seed 62 Miri each pass all three; one lookup diagnostic is deliberately ignored
in each correctness run. Nightly warnings remain.

The first musl invocation reports success but executes **zero matching tests**.
Its cached dependency fingerprint points to an older isolated source checkout;
that invocation is not validation. A dedicated fresh target executes the current
three tests successfully. The new model targets now require a three-test success
summary: a repeat against the stale target correctly fails with exit 2, while
GNU and fresh musl pass. The failed initial fixture compilation is also retained.

Shipping/speed test images complete **16 lookup-only software profiles**, four
implementations with both identical and distinct-equal string allocations.
Each executes 100,000 verified reads; binary/source checks and independent
analysis of all thirteen event totals and summed self-costs pass.

| Instructions per 100,000 same-allocation reads | Shipping | Speed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Existing generic lookup | 22,600,023 | 16,900,023 |
| String query, recomputed hash, canonical equality | 18,400,022 | 14,600,024 |
| Same query with precomputed hash | 16,200,023 | 13,200,024 |
| Precomputed hash and typed string equality | 15,200,023 | 11,600,024 |

The isolated hash saving is approximately **22 / 14 instructions per read**;
distinct-equal strings have the same deltas. Speed nevertheless adds roughly
one data write per read between the recomputed and precomputed canonical forms.
This is not a native callback timing result or evidence that instruction savings
outweigh compiler/ABI integration costs. Existing string hashes already cache
content hashing; the remaining work measured here is process-seeded key hashing.

**Do not promote or claim a regression fix from this probe.** The production
table layout, helper ABI, snapshot constants and interpreter are unchanged.
The independent benefit is small and does not establish a solution to the
callback gap. Any later native integration must retain randomized hashing,
source-bound constants, metadata/work quotas, current-table/metamethod behavior
and fresh callback state, then pass the original whole-program gates. Existing
reference snapshot payloads remain zero; they cannot be silently repurposed.
Evidence: `target/jit-evidence/short-slice-performance/prehashed-*`.

#### Descriptor/pointee alias classes — no callback benefit

Two isolated compiler trials distinguish frame-bound descriptor storage from its
canonical scalar pointees after the existing lowering proofs. Checked transport
is unchanged. They add at most two Cranelift alias regions, no readonly/notrap
claims and no persistent runtime state. Unknown stores and helpers remain
fences. Unknown loads instead skip annotation unchanged: the pinned optimizer
does not treat an unclassified load as observing every named store region.
Only separately verified private host reloads and bounded function-table reads
may remain outside the two classes. The second trial also covers the existing
verified F64 pointee-load shape; excluding it conservatively skipped functions
containing even an untaken float path.

The initial model passes **232 executions across four summaries**. Subsequent
guarded models pass four and five tests, respectively. These are separate source
revisions, not a full-suite result for the final trial. Both immutable builds
pass fmt/check-all and eleven exact-image profiles with every non-timing field
equal to array-transport. Images are

and `d0aee1195334a33b879598ea625e7ee51f84499ad1511e162397d5ad656703e5`.

by the observed 81-instruction allocator variation. Each trial adds **8,184 bytes**
to host text/data/BSS combined. No hardware speedup is claimed or timing campaign
run for this absent instruction benefit. **Do not promote either trial.**

#### Scoped SetList transport — allocation overhead reduced

`26faadb` adds a bounded fixed-list payload helper. It reads values through live
descriptors, charges the same fixed-list fuel through an exclusive fuel-field
loan, writes table elements and refreshes only the index descriptor. It does not
borrow the whole frame while sibling descriptor loans are live. Malformed bounds
and receiver/index types use the existing fallback before any fast-path effects.
Variable frames decline with the original PC/counters; overflow, partial writes,
readonly panics and stopped-helper behavior retain the original contract. The
main-checkout helper and scoped fuel API remain test-only.

Three focused differential/provenance tests cover widths 3/7/256, thirteen value
kinds, negative/overflow indices, malformed prefixes, zero/large counts, exact
fuel/PC/counters, readonly/variable frames, terminal scalar values, decline/reentry
and writes through preserved sibling pointers. Both Stacked and Tree Borrows
pass all three in both isolated and main-checkout sources. Main GNU and musl each
also pass the enlarged hybrid runtime oracle, including fixed and variable-list
table constructors with interpreter/ordinary controls, per-slice fuel/counters
and periodic GC. These are **four tests/two summaries per native platform**.
A fresh full GNU Force run on this SetList change passes **1,783 tests / 88
summaries**, zero failures and six ignored (`payload-set-list-root-gnu-all.log`).

native transport when the existing numeric-loop source planner recognizes a
region, and preserves projected/scoped/rooted/leaf/cell/activation modes. Other

planning, uses no new charged storage, and contains no benchmark names or runtime
value assumptions. A source plan does not guarantee optimization within a given
work budget; declining that optimization still leaves ordinary native code.

assumption that every specialized source/mode compiles were corrected; the latter

#### Canonical cells — native model passes; migration not approved

`1f75586` adds a test-only fixed-layout cell model targeting descriptor creation
cost at native entry. Separate typed Closure/Callback union arms avoid enlarging
the nested public `Value::Function` payload. The model preserves the existing
`(usize, i64)` size bound, including `Option<Cell>`, without inspecting `Value`
layout or converting GC references to integers. Public values, production stack
storage, native selection and resource policies are unchanged.

GNU and musl each pass seven model tests and check-all; the actual i686 fallback
toolchain passes four model tests and check-all. Five Rust-only tests pass both
Miri borrow models. The initial i686 attempt used the ordinary shell, which lacks
that target; `nix develop .#fallback` resolves it without a configuration change.
Generated code is exercised separately on the native host, not under Miri.

The generated scalar-store probe checks bounds, scalar tags and Boolean payloads
before mutation. It compares all initial value kinds, valid/refused writes,
numeric bit patterns, siblings and canonical addresses against Rust stores.
Both Rust and generated stores overwrite cells that are the only roots for
reference payloads; full collections check retention and subsequent release.
The executable module remains owned through each invocation and is then freed.
This is not integrated runtime, resource-policy or performance acceptance.
The native and Rust raw entries subsequently share the same 4,620-case matrix;
the length is read before minting the writable pointer. Both Miri models pass
that shared caller with the Rust entry, and GNU/musl rerun the actual generated
entry. The final focused lane counts remain seven/seven/four/five/five for
GNU/musl/i686/Stacked/Tree respectively, with check-all on all three targets.

**Compatibility correction:** copy-based `Stack` methods are not the entire
embedding API. `Thread::into_inner().borrow().stack()` exposes a retainable,
mutable `Gc<RefLock<Vec<Value, MetricsAlloc>>>`, even though the implementation
module is private. The existing retained-public-alias regression mutates parent
locals through that handle across callbacks and requires continued native
execution. This is also documented below under Batch integer imports.
The unchanged retained-alias regression passes again on GNU and musl.
At `1f75586`, `make jit-test JIT_MODE=force` passes 1,752 tests across 87
summaries, with six existing ignores. This is the JIT-feature workspace suite,
not the separate all-features suite or a benchmark campaign.
Replacing the canonical vector with cells would break that contract; caching
cells between entries with internal-write versioning would miss external writes.
Do not proceed with either migration on the assumption that the stack is private.
The model does not establish a compatible integration design or a speedup.

Evidence: `target/jit-evidence/short-slice-performance/canonical-cells-native-*`,
`canonical-cells-shared-*`, `canonical-cells-public-alias-*` and
`canonical-cells-force.log`.
Run `make jit-canonical-cells` and `make jit-canonical-cells-miri` for the model.
Performance work must preserve the raw-stack contract and the original workload,
native-coverage, compiled-Off and resource gates; none are waived by these tests.

#### Immutable helper dispatch fields — no callback code benefit

inside the call cannot satisfy Cranelift's whole-invocation `readonly` contract;
the installed 0.136.1 implementation and its
[API documentation](https://docs.rs/cranelift-codegen/0.136.1/cranelift_codegen/ir/struct.MemFlagsData.html#method.readonly)

#### Sparse dispatch-prefix regression fixed; callback gate still failing

`6760215` fixes a gap found by the first real selective-binding benchmark.
Source-PC masks did not include reads in the optimized dispatch prefix.
The floating loop's root guard also needs register 4; omitting it forced the
generic native path even though the source-header mask was valid. The compiler
now unions dispatch-prefix live-ins into each source-entry mask, stopping that
analysis at source headers. The independent forward checker verifies omitted
reads from both the source header and the dispatch prefix. Storage and work
remain budgeted, and native coverage is unchanged.

A new prefix-read regression failed before the fix. Seven analysis tests now
cover prefix reads, missing-mask mutations, branch definitions, cycles and
cleanup, alongside the existing four scoped ABI tests. GNU checks, the twenty
bound/read tests, the eleven-prototype audit and the sparse runtime oracle pass.
Musl passes the same analysis/ABI/bound/runtime lanes. Stacked and Tree Miri each
pass seven analysis and four ABI tests; neither executes generated native code.
These are focused checks, not a new full-suite or release acceptance claim.

- Each hardware campaign uses CPUs 0 and 16, three rotated windows, eleven

#### Selective two-word entry binding — correctness checked, timing pending

`186455d` adds a test-only `RequireSparsePayload` path on the retained two-word
payload ABI. A bounded backward dataflow computes incoming register reads for
each source entry, including both tag and payload loads. Only complete paired
scalar definitions kill requirements; helpers conservatively kill none.
An independent forward traversal rejects any omitted source read reachable
before definition. Both analyses use charged storage and bounded work.
Verified masks transfer from compiler workspace into the owning code's metadata
allocator, charging 32 bytes per source entry and releasing that storage with
the code. Unknown PCs keep full binding. Neither bytecode coverage nor helper,
fuel, PC, callback, projection or array-kernel contracts are reduced.

The original callback fixture's PC 8 requires registers 0, 1, 2, 3 and 5,
rather than all seven. This is a static requirement result, **not a speedup**.

#### Packed scalar descriptors — isolated representation model

The next structural experiment targets the retained callback wrapper's
6,030,957 descriptor-binding instructions. It does not repeat executor handoffs,
cross-callback caching, integer-prefix imports or SSA residency changes. A
test-only descriptor occupies one pointer word instead of a tag/pointer pair.
Typed Rust matches produce scalar field pointers; low two address bits
distinguish aligned Integer/Number fields. Exact immediate encodings represent
Nil, Boolean values and opaque references; no GC pointer or Rust enum layout
is exposed. Numeric fields with insufficient alignment refuse admission.

Address tagging and recovery use Rust's strict-provenance `map_addr`, not an
integer-to-pointer round trip. See the [official pointer API](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/primitive.pointer.html#method.map_addr).
Only live, correctly typed numeric descriptors may be dereferenced. Clearing a
tag does not validate an arbitrary pointer. Boolean descriptors are immediate
snapshots, so Boolean writes must replace canonical state and refresh the
destination, never silently mutate a cached Boolean. A retired Empty descriptor
may accompany a non-Nil canonical value: generic helpers must read canonical
storage in that case, not decode it as Lua nil. Replacement retires the old
destination; sibling scalar loans remain live. No descriptor may survive
callback/GC or a whole-frame borrow.

Four initial model tests pass: all fourteen Value cases, malformed immediate

budget combinations, plus malformed encodings and a zero-budget null-pointer
entry. The initial module-path error is fixed; its log is retained. GNU passes
five tests, formatting and check-all. Musl also passes five tests/check-all;
Stacked and Tree Miri each pass all four model tests, with source after-check.
The probe's deprecated mask builders are replaced with explicit unsigned and
signed-immediate APIs. The first replacement used an unsupported `u64` builder
argument; the corrected argument retains the same three-bit mask value. Initial
failed logs remain separate from final-source verification.

This is **not runtime integration or a measured speedup**. The generated probe

The follow-up implements a private bounded scope with a higher-ranked factory,
an initialized descriptor prefix (maximum 256), fresh canonical reads for retired
or opaque slots, direct same-type numeric stores, and destination-only or full
refresh. A helper marks the scope stopped and retires affected descriptors before
borrowing canonical values. A panic preserves completed canonical writes and its
original Rust payload; caught callers cannot resume that scope. Successful full
helpers bind again only after their whole-slice borrow ends.

A separate frame adapter now exercises actual `helpers::call_direct`, not just
a slice simulation. It retires every descriptor before borrowing the helper
frame and reacquires the canonical base from that frame before refreshing.
Tests check Move over all Value kinds, prior direct scalar writes, retired
destinations, prefix tails, table-read declines, invalid-register helper panics,
PC/count publication and initially pending panic payloads. A stopped scope
without a pending frame panic returns a refusal rather than fabricating a
`HELPER_PANICKED` result with no payload. This is not yet a native C bridge or
complete coverage of all ten helpers.

The initial i686 scope run reports four failed fixtures because their numeric
fields do not all satisfy the original eight-byte admission requirement. Merely
aligning the enclosing array does not fix individual fields. The protocol now
uses **two** low bits (mask 3), sufficient for Integer/Number addresses, and
reserves exact immediate addresses 2/3/4/5 for False/True/Empty/Opaque. Numeric
admission and native decoding both reject a cleared address at or below 5,
preventing Empty/Opaque from being dereferenced as numeric pointers. No Rust
Value layout is assumed, and no failing i686 test is removed or conditionally
disabled. The corrected i686 run passes all eleven then-current model tests;
the final suite adds the distinct stopped-without-frame-panic regression.

Scope source `85103de`: final GNU and musl each pass **13 tests** and check-all; GNU also passes
formatting and default/all-feature Clippy with existing warnings. Stacked and
Tree Miri each pass **12 model tests**, including real-frame reborrowing, with
unchanged source hashes. The real i686-musl executable passes all **12 model
tests**, without native execution. Initial equality/lifetime fixture compilation
failures and both failed i686 attempts remain in `packed-scope-*` logs. This
advances the helper-lifetime protocol only; whole-runtime integration,
independent emitted verification, resources and original performance gates
remain incomplete. Scope code is in `packed/scoped.rs` and `scoped_tests.rs`.

Before a C bridge can expose descriptor-array pointers, its storage must be
separate from the mutable scope control object. The current Rust-only scope owns
the array inline; retaining a pointer into that array while reborrowing the
whole owner for a helper is not covered by these passing tests. The existing
two-word runtime keeps its descriptor array separate from Session control.
Follow that lifetime separation and add Miri tests reusing the exact same array
pointer across helper calls before native integration. Current retained sibling
tests exercise scalar-field pointers, not this future descriptor-array loan.

Storage separation is implemented in `f840c21`: each factory owns its descriptor
buffer outside the mutably borrowed control object, initializes only the admitted
prefix, and retains its lifetime through a private raw pointer/capability.
An additional regression reuses the exact same array pointer across partial
replacement, retirement and full real-helper reborrows, reloading descriptors
after full refresh. GNU passes fourteen tests/check-all; both Miri alias models
pass thirteen Rust tests with source manifests unchanged.

The next packed-only C bridge provides all ten canonical helper entries behind
one unwind boundary. Its differential checks each helper's success path against

counters, PC and SetList fuel. Additional tests exercise ordinary decline with
fresh subsequent reads, real helper panics, an injected typed Rust panic,
already-pending panic and stopped state. A second attempted panic must not
replace the original payload. The descriptor array remains separate throughout.

This private bridge adds **refusal status 3**, distinct from decline 0,
completion 1 and panic 2. It records the exact refusal and stops subsequent
calls. A mutation fixture completes one real helper, then refuses refresh:
its committed PC/effects/counters remain, the next call does nothing, and the
outer Rust factory returns the refusal. It must never masquerade as ordinary
decline and replay an effect, or invent a panic result without a panic payload.
Any future packed compiler/runtime integration must handle this hard-stop
contract explicitly; the existing two-word ABI is unchanged.

A generated numeric probe writes canonical state, calls the real C gateway,
then reloads the same descriptor-array pointer and writes again **only** on
completion. Matched Rust/native fixtures cover completion, decline, panic and
post-effect refusal, verifying canonical values and exact PC/counts. This probe
has admitted numeric preconditions; it is not arbitrary-bytecode lowering,
runtime activation or independent emitted-IR certification.

The next entry contract has a **distinct return-valued function type**:
`(Packed*, pc, budget, Exit*, Bridge*) -> u32`. `RETURNED = 4` means a normal
native exit was published; gateway failure statuses are not valid normal exits.
The Rust adapter returns an explicit error for admission failure, post-execution
refusal, a declined writer, pending panic, an unexpected status or an invalid
exit. Admission failure is distinguishable from refusal after committed effects.
Neither may be silently interpreted as permission to replay the operation.
Pending panics stop admission before any native instruction, including direct
stores. The adapter bounds the budget at 64 and validates initialized exit
fields, instruction count and panic-payload consistency. A normal panic exit
retains its existing Exit reason and original frame payload.

An isolated compiler helper transformation now admits original six-argument
direct helper calls and emits five-argument calls through the packed C table.
It preserves the original result and continuation for statuses 0/1/2, but returns
status 3 before the old continuation can mistake refusal for ordinary fallback.
Independent source/emitted checks cover helper identity, arguments, signatures,
field/table offsets, the refusal predicate, branch targets and returned status.
All ten helper kinds have source/IR fixtures; eight well-formed IR mutations
are rejected. Generated full-signature entry fixtures check completion, decline,
panic, zero budget and post-effect refusal without replay or a fabricated panic.
The transformation adds seven instructions and two blocks per call; complete
compiler expansion admission still needs to account for these additions.

The wrong-type source fixture must actually construct the intended SSA type:

This generic checked lowering adds **20 instructions per tag read**, **16 per

Those costs are verified, not waived. Whole-function admission must account for

smaller descriptors. Retired Empty descriptors may represent non-Nil canonical
values: terminal-write liveness or canonical refresh must prevent native reads
from treating such a destination as Nil. This component does not establish that
whole-function invariant on its own.

Packed scalar-store lowering now admits adjacent canonical tag/bits stores and

materializing a new Value or incrementing the writer-attempt diagnostic.

Only gateway completion reaches the original continuation. Decline, panic and
refusal return their exact status before subsequent effects. Shared Rust/native

counters. Injected panic/refusal after a canonical write retain that effect and
the original panic payload; a continuation marker remains untouched. These
gateway probes do not bypass the full-entry rule that pending panics refuse
admission before executing any native instructions.

Independent source/emitted checks cover the store pair, guards, cleared pointer,

proofs. A composed fixture lowers an ordinary store, reads its refreshed tag/bits,

loop matrix proved semantic equivalence, not optimization retention. The later

optimization remains incomplete.

#### Packed failure progress and test-only runtime integration

ABI commit `1f8b23f` preserves the original helper outcome separately from
descriptor refresh. A helper that completes before refresh fails reports its
completed instruction once; a declined store or failed operation reports only
its preceding source prefix. Uninitialized, mismatched or overbudget failure
metadata is rejected rather than turned into a fabricated interpreter exit.
The original Rust panic payload remains separate from transport refusal.

Compiler commit `49cffbe` emits source-owned failure PC, prefix count and kind
on cold writer/helper failure blocks. The independent checker verifies source
ownership and each emitted field; combined source/candidate expansion includes
five additional instructions per failure site. Real generated failure probes
cover canonical writes, completed helpers followed by failed refresh and exact
counts. GNU formatting/all-feature checking and 200 broader tests passed before
runtime integration (101 ABI, 84 backend, three existing runtime, 12 helper).
The focused composition run also passed 39 packed ABI, six lowering, one progress
checker and six owning-entry tests. Logs use `packed-progress-*`.

Runtime commit `151b65c` selects the distinct packed ABI **under test-only
`RequirePackedPayload`**. Successful exits share existing PC, helper/native count,
array-prefix and panic publication. Canonical descriptors never enter the old
scalar-slot ABI or overwrite canonical state from stale scratch on return.
Transport faults stop execution: they publish only checked instruction progress
plus an already executed array prefix, preserve helper counts and canonical
effects, then resume the original panic or raise the typed internal fault.
They do not create an interpreter/guard/budget exit or replay a Lua operation.
Admission alone does not count a native entry, and unknown progress is not
invented. This follows the existing Rust-unwind fuel policy: no instruction
count returns to the executor, so this path does not introduce a new fuel charge.
It does not claim recoverable execution after an internal transport failure.

The first integrated differential passed 20 script families at eight initial
fuel values, comparing the packed candidate against ordinary JIT and interpreter
through repeated steps, interrupts, callback/upvalue activity, collection, array
kernels and exact counters. The expanded suite additionally covers debug hooks,
all 256 initialized register prefixes, zero-register/unknown-PC entry and
five injected failure outcomes through the actual runtime dispatch. Injected
ABI failure probes and compiler-generated failure probes are separate evidence.
Publisher tests cover saturation, original payloads, PC and array-prefix counts.
Expanded GNU and musl suites each pass **205 tests** (101 ABI, 86 backend,
five consuming-runtime, one failure-publisher, 12 helper). The focused native
entry target passes eight tests, including zero-register and injected runtime
failure dispatch. Real i686 passes 35 packed ABI tests without a native compiler.
Formatting, all-feature checking and default/all-feature Clippy pass, with
warnings; Clippy reports 190 library-test warnings including the new bridge
report tuple-complexity warning. Both Stacked and Tree Borrows Miri pass 35 packed
ABI, four pure whole-lowering and one progress-checker test; the complete source
manifest matches afterward. Native runtime execution is not run under Miri.
Logs use `packed-runtime-*`, and targets include `jit-payload-packed-runtime`.

#### Packed integer-loop optimization retention

ABI commit `56e168b` distinguishes a completed optimized checkpoint from an
ordinary pre-instruction failure. Only checkpoint failure admits a completed
count equal to the budget; store/helper pre-instruction failures keep their
strict bound. A checkpoint cannot borrow a helper completion record.

Compiler commit `f970d90` restores the original integer-loop augmentation for
packed entries. The existing independent integer-loop verifier produces a
private region certificate. Checkpoint admission rechecks each complete flush,
typed parameters, stores, memory flags and outgoing arguments before supplying
its source PC/count. The completed-loop flush has a constant next PC; the budget
flush carries a dynamic PC and completed count. Neither is assigned an arbitrary
ordinary instruction owner. Original source ownership still governs all ordinary
operations, and helpers cannot claim a loop checkpoint certificate.

Failure emission uses four instructions for a dynamic PC and five for a constant
PC. Prepublication admission and the whole-function checker account for the exact
additional size before mutation. The test-only code object records whether the
optimization was installed, and the exhaustive four-loop integer/float,
ascending/descending matrix now requires that fact before comparing every entry,
budget and invalid scalar guard against optimized ordinary code.

Focused GNU checks pass 40 packed ABI, six whole-lowering, two progress-checker,
one integer-checkpoint and eight owning native-entry tests. Mutation tests reject
changed flush constants/stores/branch arguments and emitted PC/count/kind fields.
The initial pure fixture needed the default memory-flag table already present in
real ordinary IR; the preservation verifier was not relaxed. Failed API/borrow
and fixture attempts are retained in `packed-loop-*` logs. GNU and musl each pass
the 207-test core payload/runtime/helper suite, the seven original integer-loop
tests, the new checkpoint test and repeated focused lowering/progress checks.
Real i686 passes 36 packed ABI tests. Formatting, all-feature checking and both
Clippy modes pass with warnings (191 library-test warnings, including the new
progress-method argument-count warning). Both Stacked and Tree Borrows Miri pass
36 packed ABI, four whole-lowering, two progress and one integer-checkpoint test.
All 368 source-manifest entries match after validation. Native code execution is
covered by GNU/musl, not Miri; these checks do not establish a speedup.

#### Packed scoped helper fast paths

The packed prototype now has destination-local upvalue reads, constant-key local
and closed-upvalue table reads, table writes and table allocation. These retain
the legacy payload fast cases without retiring and rebuilding unrelated scalar
descriptors. Unhandled operations still use the full-frame helper path, retiring
all descriptors first and refreshing control/value pointers before rebinding.
Retired Empty operands are read from canonical state rather than treated as nil.
Current-stack aliases, foreign/closed upvalues, table guards and helper counters
remain subject to the original helper semantics.

Helper completion is recorded after the canonical destination write and before
descriptor refresh. An allocation/foreign-stack panic before the write remains
uncompleted; a failure after a completed write cannot cause replay. The outer
bridge retains the original panic payload and forbids further helper/writer
execution. Control metadata is captured before scalar binding and refreshed after
full-frame fallback; fast operations do not borrow the whole canonical frame.

Native focused checks pass 48 packed ABI tests, including eight new fast-path
tests covering all value kinds, sibling pointer read/write permission, initialized
prefixes, current/foreign aliases, expired/locked stacks, read/write guards,
constants, retired values and original panic identity/single destruction.
An initial Stacked Borrows smoke test found a real pointer-ancestry error:
capturing control metadata through the original mutable frame invalidated its
saved sibling pointer. Setup now derives subsequent borrows through the retained
parent pointer. The corrected three-test smoke passes; the initial failed log is
retained. Full GNU and musl checks each pass 215 payload/runtime/helper tests.
Stacked and Tree Borrows each pass all 44 pure packed ABI tests, and i686 passes
the same 44 tests. Formatting, check-all and GNU Clippy pass (Clippy still reports
191 lib-test warnings). All 370 frozen source entries match after validation.
Logs are retained in `packed-fast-*`. These are test-only implementation results,
not a speedup claim.

#### Original-workload read audit

`make jit-payload-read-audit` now inspects generated IR after the ordinary
integer-loop augmentation and stops before native code emission. It traverses
all nine original workload sources, including both child prototypes (11 total),
and verifies mapping, compiler metadata, and snapshot workspace cleanup.
The first audit finds 94 scalar payload reads: 69 are already admitted by the
masked-numeric proof. No candidate fails its dominance/use admission.

Ten further reads are concrete optimization witnesses: the integer and float
loop entries each load five fields after a conjunction of exact numeric tag
checks. Their tag loads are not adjacent to their field loads, and the guards
precede those loads, so merely adding exact equality to the current forward
recognizer would not admit them. The other 15 reads remain unclassified by this
audit; Move/truthiness payloads must not be assumed numeric. Next is a separately
verified in-place bound-read path using fresh exact-tag guards. No new read
lowering or performance gain is claimed by this audit. Full IR and counts are
in `target/jit-evidence/short-slice-performance/payload-read-audit-validation.log`.

Commit `7fc1231` implements that separate path for frame-bound entries. A read
stays at its original instruction, with only a descriptor-pointer load inserted

write checker requires the exact retiring gateway when liveness selects it.

image in the same windows; CPU16 remains 0.9751–0.9965. The candidate still fails

Retain the cold annotation only in the test model, with exact emitted-policy
validation and a mutation test rejecting cold annotations on generic writes.
Generic type-changing materializers remain unmarked. The no-trap hint stays

The next structural step must use an explicitly frame-bound entry contract,
not remove null checks from the existing raw-descriptor ABI. Introduce a private,
non-escaping binding capability minted only inside the canonical frame/session
scope, and a distinct compiler/entry kind that cannot use scratch-slot or linked
entry invocation. Keep all checked-descriptor entry tests, including malformed
numeric/null inputs, unchanged. For that separate entry kind, a fresh proven
numeric destination can use its Rust-bound scalar field directly without a
redundant malformed-pointer materializer path. Source and emitted CFG proofs,
exact expansion accounting, helper refresh, terminal retirement, native exit
state and both Miri models remain mandatory. No binding or native frame may
survive callback/GC or a whole-frame helper borrow. Start with existing full-entry
lowering, not a new per-span dispatcher, and measure the original workload matrix
before activation. This separate capability/entry contract is not implemented
or accepted yet; the checked ABI cannot be weakened in its place.

Target the ordinary wrapper's **12,321,657 import/writeback instructions**,
not another tiny scalar-guard or rejected callback-setup/cache variation.
Generic direct-payload transport already exists as an unaccepted model, but
still pays dynamic tag/pointer checks and descriptor materialization/rebinding.
The new direction is source-certified typed regions with Rust-side admission,
direct access to admitted scalar fields, and canonical terminal stores that
retire descriptors rather than rebuilding a value that will not be read again.

The initial model selects distinct integer cells through ordinary Rust matches;
it never reads the private representation of `Value`. Replacements, including
Integer-to-Integer replacement, invalidate only the selected destination.
Refresh rechecks its current type before making that binding live again.
Unselected GC values and retained sibling scalar pointers remain untouched.
Bindings are scoped to the canonical borrow and may not survive callbacks,
collection or whole-frame helper access. No production transport is changed.

The initial six GNU tests and fmt/check-all pass. Tests cover invalid/duplicate selections,
all Value kinds, NaN bits, widths 0/1/7/255/256, sparse/reverse selection,
unwind visibility and fresh admission. An executable Cranelift probe performs
a typed integer add and a terminal canonical scalar store via a Rust leaf;
native code treats the `Value` destination as opaque. Its independent oracle
checks **500 schedules** (25 integer pairs, four destinations including both
selected aliases, five budgets), exact completed work and descriptor retirement.
The same ABI protocol has a Rust simulation for Miri; native execution is not
Miri coverage. Initial comparison/GC-lifetime compile errors remain in the logs.

Foundation validation also passes Stacked/Tree Miri (five tests each), musl
(six typed, 28 payload ABI, 28 backend, two runtime tests), and i686 (five
model tests), all without failures or ignores. Native execution remains
excluded under Miri and unsupported architectures.

A source-backed test-only plan now admits bounded straight-line integer
Add/Sub/Mul/Minus/Move/LoadConstant spans from verified bytecode snapshots.
Only read-before-definition inputs need typed admission. Subsequent reads
refer to their exact reaching definition; writes to admitted cells use the
typed field, while other destinations use canonical replacement and are
never read through a retired field pointer. This permits reuse of computed
results without rebuilding descriptors. Every operation still writes its
canonical destination before an exit. No helper, branch or callback crosses
the region, and a fuel stop requires fresh admission for a suffix.

An independently traversed source-plan verifier checks operand provenance,
binding uniqueness/use, destinations, stores, constants and the 64-operation
cap. Plan storage uses the existing budget allocator, with exact-limit and
failed-allocation cleanup tests. Prefix/suffix oracles cover wrapping extrema,
aliasing, same-type and type-changing destinations, and unselected GC values;
compiler-generated arithmetic spans are covered too. GNU now passes ten
typed tests plus fmt/check-all. This verifies the plan/model, not emitted IR
or integration with runtime fuel/counters. Source-plan initial module-path
failure and corrected output are retained in `typed-source-plan-*.log`.

The next test-only lowering emits native code from these verified plans,
instead of a manually specified two-operation probe. It caches admitted field
pointers and SSA results, writes canonical state at each instruction, and
checks the remaining operation budget before each body. The code owner borrows
the immutable plan used for admission and frees executable memory on drop.
Tests compare all prefixes of every suffix of the arithmetic fixture and a
real compiler-generated span against a separate bytecode oracle. The boundary
corpus includes 64 operations, register 255, wrong-type no-write admission,
plan corruption before compilation, and a zero-budget native call with null
tables proving no table access on that path.

GNU passes **12 typed tests** and fmt/check-all; both Miri models and real i686
pass **nine model tests each**. The completed musl lane passes **12 typed,
34 payload ABI, 28 backend and two runtime tests**. Every lane reports zero
failures and ignores. Miri does not execute the generated machine code.
At this stage the emitter still lacked independent post-lowering semantic IR
certification, production executable/compiler resource accounting, runtime
PC/fuel/counter integration, branch/helper coverage, and whole-workload
performance evidence. Generic Cranelift verification and the executable
oracle do not replace those gates. Do not activate or call this a speedup.
Native immediate-type compilation failure and corrected results are retained
under `typed-source-native-*.log`.

The next change adds an independent, bounded post-lowering checker before
native definition. It revalidates the source plan, validates the C ABI,
restricts the control-flow graph to one guarded body per source operation,
and checks exact unsigned budgets and completed counts. Every body must have
one final canonical or typed write matching its source expression. Pointer
loads must come from admitted binding entries or initialized canonical
destination entries; scalar reads may only dereference admitted fields.
The checker does not regenerate and compare the emitter's output. Its fixed
workspace and graph-size caps reject extra blocks, detached instructions and
oversized IR before structural verification.

Fourteen GNU typed tests plus fmt/check-all pass. A corruption corpus rejects
at least 70 variants that still pass Cranelift's generic verifier, including
wrong offsets/roots/values, signed budgets, reversed edges, loops, writer
redirection, wrong helper arguments/ABI, pre-budget reads and extra writes.
Changed source constants, function ABI and capacity overflow are also refused.
The existing executable prefix/suffix and boundary corpora now pass through
this checker. The emitter reuses each budget-count constant in its comparison.
Compiler API and mutable-borrow errors from the initial checker drafts remain
in `typed-ir-initial.log` and `typed-ir-corrected.log`; the passing run is
`typed-ir-mutations.log`. No production activation or speedup is claimed.

The completed checker musl lane passes 14 typed, 36 payload ABI, 28 backend
and two runtime tests. A further source-map test imports the unchanged
benchmark workload definitions, traverses their child prototypes, and reports
potential integer spans and excluded operations. GNU now passes 15 typed
tests plus fmt/check-all. This is static source admission, not dynamic type
coverage or performance evidence; for example a Move of a closure is a
potential span whose integer admission will decline at runtime.

The map determines the integration direction. `rust_callbacks` has GetUpTable
at PC5, Move at PC6, Call at PC7, Add at PC8 and NumericForLoop at PC9. Its
current hot scalar spans are only `6..7` and `8..9`. The upvalue callee is
GetUpValue/Add/SetUpValue/Return, with only its Add in the scalar model.
**Do not install separate per-span dispatch for these fragments:** it would
leave the existing import/writeback path and introduce transitions, so this
is not a justified way to remove the measured copying cost. Instead integrate
typed accesses within the existing canonical payload execution path, with
source-certified loop flow and closed helper effects, exact retirement of
overwritten bindings, and full ordinary fallback. This direction is an
inference from current source and the earlier profiles, not a measured gain.
Retain the scalar model as a verified component, not as narrower acceptance.
The clean single-threaded map is `typed-workload-boundaries-final.log`; its
initial allocator-box iteration error and first corrected run are retained.
The final map-inclusive platform checks pass 15 typed tests on musl and ten
on real i686, with zero failures or ignores (`typed-ir-musl-final.log` and
`typed-ir-i686.log`). The native IR checker and its mutations do not execute
under Miri or i686; the prior nine-model Miri results are not checker coverage.

Before activation, require: both Miri alias models; source-certified region and
binding maps; independent IR/liveness/retirement verification and corruption
tests; exact budgets/exits/helper/counter behavior; bounded compiler/runtime
accounting and refusal; integration with current fallback/callback/GC contracts;
whole-profile savings and unchanged repeated native/feature-cost gates.
The two-operation probe is **not** a complete compiler pass, release integration
or performance result. Ordinary production remains the byte-restored baseline.
Evidence: `target/jit-evidence/short-slice-performance/typed-payload-region-*`.

#### Typed scalar payload boundary — test-only (2026-10-10)

The next structural experiment supplies pointers to scalar fields from Rust,
rather than teaching generated code the layout of `Value`. The scoped model
exposes integer, number and Boolean payloads; nil and reference variants have
null pointers. Canonical helper reads and writes rebind the accessed descriptor,
and the native caller reloads descriptors after each helper. Whole-frame mutable
reborrows, callback/suspension lifetimes, relocation and collection are not
permitted while these pointers are live.

Five tests pass on GNU x86_64, musl x86_64 and fallback i686, and under pinned
Miri with both Stacked and Tree Borrows. They cover scalar bits/type changes,
reference identity, partial writes during unwinding, and an original-pointer
extern-C gateway. The gateway exercises aliased source/destination moves,
descriptor rebinding, bounds refusal and caught helper panic without unwinding
across C. Miri warnings are retained in the raw logs.

This is not a production ABI change or measured speedup. Existing native code
still uses scalar scratch slots. Generated-code lowering, real helper/upvalue
integration, root/barrier handling, bounded resources and whole-profile cost
acceptance remain unproven. In particular, the model does not authorize keeping
canonical payload pointers across any existing callback or collection boundary.

`target/jit-evidence/short-slice-performance/payload-gateway-*`.

(`481eb5b2548d9ed8b684bb5d803a2786583db0e04d079ed6303ec9b0b1b5a87c`).

#### Sign-directed checked jump arithmetic — withdrawn (2026-10-10)

On the restored runtime, a source trial replaces `checked_add_signed` with
negative-offset `checked_sub(offset.unsigned_abs())` and nonnegative-offset

Two bucket offsets replace cached entry pointers and duplicated keys, occupying

index borrow. No persistent mutable-pointer provenance or interior mutability
is needed. Policy, weak source identity, recency, ownership and counters remain
unchanged.

ten ignored. An initial cold-hash prototype failed Miri lookups because ahash's

does not establish shipping enablement or performance acceptance.

#### Rooted atomic publication — measured development WIP, not accepted

`534344f` introduces a test-only rooted caller model and native differential;
`0676a7a` extends it through native-region continuation and panic recovery.
`976ca11` enables the checked path, `907f416` inlines its snapshot/window helpers,
and `ca1ba5a` combines caller publication and continuation checks in one register
borrow. The final version is retained as **experimental development WIP**, not
release acceptance: it improves native calls and restores speed-profile numeric
performance, but a substantial shipping-profile float regression remains.

Immutable typed roots preserve reference identity while validated scalar/reference
slots represent pending caller values. The existing verified compact native entry
still computes the integer result. Complete argument shifting, nil-filled tails,
overlapping callee temporaries, captures, PC, fuel and logical Call/Return counters
are reproduced. The caller is published once after each atomic call, **before any
next generated caller entry**; no full canonical recapture is needed on success.
Refusal publishes pending caller state and retains physical fallback. Panic
recovery publishes pending state while preserving the pre/post-commit canonical PC.
Source/type/capture/hook/frame/depth/capacity/fuel checks remain; there is no new
unsafe code, allocation, persistent capture cache or native coverage reduction.

The pure model covers 648 call-layout combinations and every scalar/reference
kind, including NaN bits, negative zero, moved root aliases and short-destination
refusal without mutation. Native differentials cover 720 paired cases, pending
values, repeated virtual calls and captures in an upper physical frame. Region
tests explicitly count rooted completions and compare bounded execution/fuel;
faults before and after atomic commit verify canonical publication and counters.
An initial fault-fixture expectation incorrectly excluded already completed caller
dispatches; the corrected assertion compares that work to the interpreter without
prematurely charging fuel. Failed logs are retained.

The slot model passes **three Miri tests**. Initial native Memcheck passes **41
region tests** (two ignored) and **two direct rooted tests**, zero errors and zero
definite/indirect leaks. Final publication panic and bounded-region fixtures also
pass native Memcheck. The usual 48 possibly-lost/632 reachable harness bytes remain.
Each refinement passes GNU checking and **1,566 focused/all-feature Auto executions
across 105 suites**, eight ignored; 169/18 are focused gates. Initial baseline,
all-feature Auto and documentation runs additionally pass **1,817/176**, ten
ignored. These are test executions, including overlapping suites, not distinct
test counts or new platform certification.

Three independently frozen variants each complete two native and two three-way
speed/shipping cost rounds: **288 aggregate commands total, all failing unchanged
aggregate gates**. All **648 native non-timing pairs** match, including execution
and resource counters. Each round retains three alternating/rotating windows on

tests and profiles terminate before timing. Source/image manifests and exact
symbol companions verify. All variants' no-feature executables are byte-identical
to their immediate controls.

#### Atomic integer-call transitions — retained structural development WIP

`c7b540d` first prototypes, and `a7def2c` expands tests for, executing a complete
source-verified integer callee without constructing a physical callee frame.
`fa90638` enables this path for admitted calls. The existing generated compact
integer function still performs the arithmetic; Rust does not substitute its
answer or count interpreted arithmetic as native work.

This deliberately refines the earlier unconditional physical-Call/Return
implementation, not the Lua execution contract. Elision requires a fixed caller
with no pending return, the exact live closure/prototype/source binding, fixed
arguments within parameter bounds, integer inputs, an integer capture strictly
below the callee tail, existing frame/value capacities and room below the depth
limit. Open captures or close markers in that tail refuse. The fuel remainder
after Call and the caller prefix must allow execution to continue; the native
budget must cover the complete three-operation payload. Hook and mode guards
remain, and custom fault-hook fixtures use the physical path.

All validation and native computation precede publication. Successful publication
reproduces argument shifting, nil-filled callee registers, native read/result
temporaries, capture writes, complete caller stack height, PC, fuel and logical
Call/Return dispatch accounting. Even otherwise-dead overlapping caller slots
are preserved. There is no allocation, new unsafe code, GC pointer in generated
arithmetic, retained stack pointer or persistent capture-route cache. Any refusal
retains canonical physical execution and its partial/error/suspension behavior.

The differential covers **1,536 paired scenarios**, with **86 actual atomic native
completions**, comparing full physical-state traces, interruption and eight
execution counters. Other cases exercise unchanged physical fallback. Dedicated
tests cover captures in an upper physical frame, 256-register capacity refusal,
argument-tail capture rebinding and 21 host refusal/precommit-panic cases.
`make jit-atomic-call` exposes these tests. Existing source-binding tests caught
an initial unwanted registry reborrow; atomic admission now consumes the already
bound caller/prototype identity and still resolves the live closure and capture.
The prototype's initial two-dispatch report incorrectly counted one interpreted
slice; separate Call/Return reports and the expanded counter differential fix it.
Initial command/fixture failures remain with corrected terminal validation logs.

Focused production checks pass **161 executions / 16 suites**, two ignored.
Baseline/doc/all-feature Auto passes **1,808 executions / 173 suites**, eight
ignored. Three native differentials pass Memcheck with zero errors and zero
definite/indirect leaks; 48 possibly-lost and 632 reachable harness bytes remain.
This is GNU evidence, not a new full platform certification.

Exact-image upvalue work falls **251,705,217 → 191,970,307 instructions (23.7%)**.
Two native and two three-way speed/shipping cost rounds complete **96 commands**;
all fail unchanged aggregate gates. All **216 native non-timing pairs** match,
including execution/resource counters, and pre/post manifests and exact symbol
companions verify. Runs retain three alternating/rotating windows on CPU0/16,
eleven samples, twenty cost iterations and external contention. No owned build,
test or profile overlaps timing.

Native upvalue control/candidate throughput ratios improve **1.372127 / 1.379452**
on CPU0 and **1.295656 / 1.307775** on CPU16, first / repeat. However, the native
speedup against its own interpreter is only **1.0752–1.1607**, below the original
**1.25** target in every candidate window. Numeric native targets, helper-heavy
targets and disabled-cost controls are not waived.

**Regressions remain explicit:** CPU16 native float ratios are

#### Guarded integer-loop region — earlier test-only prototype measurements

The new experiment keeps a separate typed loop graph alongside the entire
generic native graph instead of transporting scalar state through arbitrary-PC
joins. It recognizes bounded contiguous Add/Sub/Mul/Move/integer-constant bodies
ending in NumericForLoop: at most 32 operations, sixteen frame registers and
eight region registers. Fresh PC, nonzero-fuel and integer-tag guards control
entry; incompatible values retain the original implementation. Every source
opcode still checks fuel. Budget exits flush mutable state, and loop completion
rejoins the original suffix with the accumulated logical count.

The initial version improves integer control/candidate throughput
**2.183416 / 2.131504 on CPU16**. CPU0 shows **2.613977 / 1.821089**, alongside
large reversed noninteger timing movement that is preserved, not filtered.
The refined version requires conservative source-known integer initialization
as an eligibility filter, avoiding a useless fast region for dynamic arithmetic
inputs. It does **not** replace live tag guards or reduce generic native coverage.

The refined version repeats integer gains of **1.797425 / 1.799825 on CPU0**
and **2.106078 / 2.206807 on CPU16**. All twelve refined candidate windows pass
the unchanged integer **2× interpreter** gate, with ratios **2.4256–3.4500**.
Profiled generated integer self-instructions fall from **22,000,801 to
6,587,558**. These are measurements of experimental binaries, not a speedup
already enabled in the committed production runtime.

Other results are not universally positive: refined CPU16 table throughput is
**0.987644 / 0.978808**, polymorphic **0.981513 / 0.971405**; CPU0 upvalue is
**0.977752 / 0.989104** and predicate **0.990940 / 0.985873**. Across the two
variants, four full native comparisons retain **48 commands / 1,296 reported
rows** on CPUs 0/16, three alternating windows and eleven samples. All aggregate
commands still fail unchanged gates. All **432 paired case rows** match in
non-timing fields, including native/logical/helper counters and resources.
No feature-cost or full performance acceptance is claimed.

Both experimental variants pass **1,592 executions / 115 suites**, zero failures
and six existing ignores. `make jit-integer-loop`, included in `jit-tags`, checks
source recognition/refusal and actual generated execution against the boundary
model for three loop bodies, every entry, extreme integer values and nine
budgets. A separate native probe confirms fast entry and nil/boolean/float,
zero-budget and unknown-PC fallback. Overflow stores the wrapped internal index
without incorrectly changing the visible variable; direct zero-step latch
entry preserves the original bounded semantics. Mappings are reclaimed.

At that measurement checkpoint the implementation was **test-only**, requiring explicit
`RequireIntegerLoop` or `ProbeIntegerLoop` selection. Production activation was
removed until an independent checker validated the new region, its source
binding, unchanged generic graph and exact guards/state transfers, with mutation
and resource-bound tests. Cranelift structural verification and model examples
alone are not that translation proof. The independent checker and fresh
native/feature-cost comparisons are now recorded above. Full-plan
resource/platform/release gates remain open.
`00f31e8` retains the prototype and native-entry/model tests. The restored
format/check/focused/baseline/all-feature Auto/doc run passes **2,005 executions
/ 202 suites**, zero failures and ten existing ignores.
The freshly rebuilt restored native benchmark has identical `.text` to the
frozen control. Whole images differ in 46 u32 words, with deltas of 8 and 70
matching source-line movement; before/after hashes pass. No new restored
feature-cost build or whole-image identity is claimed.

non-memory trapping instructions and unsupported terminators refuse the pass.

and unchanged refusal. This is not an independent translation proof.

#### Lazy numeric-loop limit checks — retained development WIP

`39dfdce` branches on the freshly guarded limit tag inside the integer
index/step path. It executes only the applicable integer or floating limit
comparison instead of eagerly evaluating both. The floating index/step path,
integer overflow handling, result tags, canonical stores, logical fuel,
physical calls/returns and fallback remain unchanged. The exact loop verifier
checks the new nested split and three incoming arms; numeric-input obligations
increase from six to seven, with the additional record/storage fully charged.

New model differential coverage executes **292,008 generated invocations**:
23 index/limit/step values, including integer extremes, precision boundaries,
signed zero, subnormal, infinities, NaN and nonnumeric refusals; two register
bases, three entry PCs and four budgets. Exit PCs, reasons, logical counts and
all register values match. Six added backend mutations reject wrong nested
targets, constant conditions, unrelated tag sources, mixed-arm phi/overflow
corruption and duplicate incoming edges before code generation/mapping.
Final focused format/check/tags/numeric gates pass **199 executions / 22 suites**;
baseline/all-feature Auto/docs pass **1,765 / 172**, ten ignored.
No new Miri or supported-platform acceptance is claimed.

**24,839,482 → 22,000,801** instructions and float **21,429,217 → 19,106,650**.
Total work falls **32,356,270 → 29,517,589** and
**28,973,136 → 26,650,569**; leading VM/invoke/Executor self-work is unchanged.
Symbol companions match original program headers and allocated bytes.
These profiles support the selected optimization; simulated instruction counts
are not hardware-performance acceptance.

#### Masked native numeric guards — retained development WIP

`9aa2e25` replaces `(tag == INTEGER) || (tag == NUMBER)` with the equivalent
full-width `(tag & !1) == INTEGER`; a compile-time assertion checks the tag
adjacency/alignment. No guard is omitted, hoisted, cached or moved across a
write/helper boundary. The bounded tag verifier now evaluates I64 AND literals
under its existing shared 64-node condition budget, resolves aliases, and
retains conservative unknown handling. Other tag/Boolean/source/effect proofs,
logical fuel, helpers, physical transitions and canonical exits are unchanged.

Exact current-image profiling selected generated code rather than another host
wrapper trial: integer Auto had 28,718,517 generated instructions out of
36,235,414 total; float had 26,114,750 out of 33,658,669. The new guard lowers
these to **24,839,482 / 32,356,270** and **21,429,217 / 28,973,136**,
respectively. VM, invoke and Executor leading self-work is unchanged. Exact
upvalue work falls 258,058,676 → 256,103,715; allocation 34,689,196 →
34,172,816. Symbol companions match program headers and allocated bytes of
the original-flag executables. Instruction/cache simulations are diagnostics,
not independent hardware explanations or acceptance.

New verifier fixtures admit both branch polarities and bounded nested masks;
they reject wider scalar sets, unrelated queried sources and depth exhaustion.
Actual generated add/subtract/multiply execute **3,072 invocations** over
sixteen adversarial tags per operand and four budgets. High-bit tags sharing
numeric low bits must decline without effects; valid tags retain exact result
types, PCs, logical counts and budget/fallback exits. `make jit-input` runs
these together with omitted-guard refusal tests. Focused format/check/tags/numeric
gates pass **192 executions / 22 suites**. Baseline/all-feature Auto/docs pass
**1,758 / 172**, ten ignored. No new Miri or supported-platform acceptance is
claimed for this checkpoint.

#### Direct primitive arithmetic — retained development WIP

`0a01bb3` adds typed integer/number/mixed-tag paths to shared `meta_ops` add,
subtract and multiply. Integer arithmetic wraps; mixed inputs use the same
integer-to-float cast and operand order as before. Nonnumeric operands retain
the original constant-coercion/metamethod/error path. Constant folding and
public conversion methods do not change. There is no feature-dependent semantic
branch, changed native source admission, reduced coverage or relaxed threshold.

This follows exact-image investigation of the preceding compact ABI. Shipping
integer/float instruction totals and VM attribution were identical before and
after that change; full-worker VM self-work was also identical. Those profiles
do not explain its timing losses or establish a hardware cause. They expose
costly Value-to-Constant handling and string-capable normalization for operands
already known to be numeric. Direct typed arithmetic removes that work.

New differential coverage performs **55,779 operator evaluations per test**
against unchanged Constant operations: integer extremes and rounding boundaries,
all numeric tag pairings, signed zero, subnormals, infinities/NaNs, numeric and
invalid strings. Float bits match except NaN payloads, compared by category.
An integrated fixture checks both metamethod operand orders and invalid operand
errors. Focused no-feature/JIT Off/Auto/Force checks pass **82 executions / six
suites**. Baseline/all-feature Auto/docs pass **1,756 / 172**, ten ignored.
The initial test mistakenly compared `Value` with `PartialEq`; its compile
failure is retained and corrected by explicit variant comparison before these
gates. No new platform or Miri acceptance is claimed.

#### Compact callee value ABI — retained development WIP

`a56939c` replaces the private four-pointer compact ABI with two `i64` inputs
and one `i64` result. Generated code still executes the recognized arithmetic;
typed host state preserves GetUpValue/SetUpValue aliases and repeated prepared
frame invocation. There is no generated memory indexing in this kernel. Source
binding, register bounds/types, live code ownership, fresh capture/source
guards, canonical materialization, physical Call/Return, panic transport, fuel
and native accounting remain. No capture-route cache or reduced coverage was
introduced. The generic fallback and custom-hook path are unchanged.

The exhaustive arithmetic/register/capture/wrapping matrix now checks three
successive invocations per prepared frame: **3,888 scenarios / 7,776 native
invocations** across direct and cached entries. Obsolete generated-memory-offset
mutations are replaced by return-flow mutation; subtraction operand, signature,
source and binding-identity rejection remain. Focused GNU checks pass **113
executions / eight suites**, two ignored. Baseline, all-feature Auto and docs
pass **1,752 / 172**, ten ignored. Five compact tests pass Memcheck with zero
errors and zero definite/indirect leaks; it reports 48 possibly-lost bytes in
Rust thread initialization and 544 reachable bytes, not a zero-allocation exit.
A test-only mutable-borrow compilation failure during return-mutation coverage
was corrected before these final gates. Rebuilt native and both cost-profile
images match the frozen candidate byte-for-byte after the correction.

Exact-image whole-executor profiling decreases upvalue instruction count
**265,953,552 → 257,914,304** (3.02%). Admission invocation self-work decreases
68,441,030 → 63,100,226 and compact preparation 7,375,396 → 5,467,966.
The symbol companion has matching program headers and allocated section bytes.
Simulated instruction-cache events worsen; neither simulation nor instruction
count identifies a hardware cause or substitutes for wall-clock measurements.

#### Unified hook/native dispatch — retained development WIP

The VM now selects hooked, observing, compiled or plain interpretation once
per slice. Hook dispatch is part of that state rather than a second hot-loop
check. Native execution and hooks retain their existing bodies, with one
interpreter loop, independent test-only resume/mock handling and unchanged
fuel, source admission, physical transitions, statistics and code ownership.
Plain no-feature interpretation uses the same two hook states. Both speed and
shipping no-feature `.text` sections remain byte-identical to the controls;
full-file hashes differ and are retained with their own matched controls.

Exact speed-image profiles identify a structural reduction: whole-executor
integer instructions fall **22,843,840 → 21,903,015** (4.12%); float falls
**30,245,910 → 29,504,975** (2.45%). VM self-work accounts for the reductions.
The symbol companions match allocated bytes and program headers of the actual
timing images. These instruction counts do not establish hardware speedups.

Two complete comparisons use all nine native cases and both disabled-cost

All **72 aggregate commands / 1,080 reported rows** remain failed; this is

#### Packed reference-prefix snapshot — rejected

Packing only reference values into a private active prefix passed 71 focused
executions and five Miri model tests, but increased exact native upvalue work
from **265,823,119 to 267,498,369** instructions. Initial upvalue direct ratios
were 0.9904/0.9939 on CPU0/16; repeat ratios were 1.0163/1.0165. CPU16 native
array and CPU0 compiled-Off float regressed in both complete comparisons.
All 24 aggregate commands / 648 rows failed, with native/resource counters
unchanged. The production trial was removed; the retained root-rebinding and
density regression test is committed separately as `88795dc`. Restored checks
pass 70 executions / seven suites. Full trial patches and measurements remain
under `packed-roots-*`; the scoped reference Move implementation below remains
the authoritative native backend.

#### Scoped reference-index moves — retained development WIP

`4de2044` removes Rust helper crossings for reference Moves in source-certified
native callers. Generated code copies tag/index pairs referring to a bounded
typed snapshot, never GC pointers or Rust enum layouts. The snapshot stays inside the
activation's arena mutation and is rebuilt after canonical transitions. Callers
with reference constants or other native helpers keep their original backend;
no native workload is disabled. Physical Call/Return, fresh admission guards,
full materialization, fuel and panic transport remain.

Transfer verification checks exact source/payload/destination, continuation and
instruction count; helper verification rejects any generated call in this mode.
Tests cover closure copies after overwriting their original slot, every value
kind and register boundaries, malformed indices/tags, every native entry/budget,
and corrupt source/destination/payload/ownership/continuation rejection.

**1.0856/1.0300**, then **1.0689/1.0385**. Exact-image work falls from 276,871,067
to 265,823,119 instructions (3.99%). Logical native work remains **778,484**;
helper-backed work falls from **134,406 to 5,132**. Only live/peak owner metadata
changes, by eight bytes, among the other reported counters. Mappings remain
28,672 bytes. This is structural progress, not full performance acceptance.

**Tradeoffs remain unresolved.** Native-harness CPU0 compiled-Off integer and
callback timings regress on repeat (ratios 0.9079/0.8875). A separate full

below 1.25. Keeping the development candidate is not approval of these
regressions or permission to release it; disabled cost and the remaining native

#### Signed jump domain and disabled-cost diagnosis — implemented, gates open

Exact original-flag speed cost executables were rebuilt with linker-symbol
replays. Rebuilds match the frozen pre-call-change and fixed-call binaries;
every loaded section and program header matches its symbol replay. Their
compiled-Off integer profiles both execute 23,343,705 instructions; float
profiles both execute 30,745,755. Dynamic read/write counts also match. The VM
has 10,903 identical address-normalized assembly instructions and unchanged
0xd40b size, but moves from 0x590550 to 0x590b30. This rules out extra executed
VM work in these workloads; it does not establish a hardware timing cause.
Hardware performance counters were unavailable, and no system setting changed.

Inspection of the hot jump helper found two real signed-domain bugs. The
compiler converted a backward distance to positive i16 before negation, so it
rejected -32768. The interpreter negated i16 before widening, overflowing for
that same valid offset. Compiler differences now use checked wide arithmetic;
the interpreter uses checked_add_signed, matching existing JIT/model behavior.
Tests exhaust every i16 offset at boundary PCs, retain invalid overflow/
underflow rejection, and compile/run a Lua loop with an actual -32768 backedge
and 32,767 additions. Both no-feature and JIT builds execute that regression.

All 113 focused executions pass, with two ignored. The GNU baseline, full
all-feature Auto, and documentation validation run passes 1,738 executions
across 172 suites, with ten ignored. Commit 74c29d1 contains the correctness
fix; it is retained independently of performance acceptance.

The new native screen contains 324 rows against the fixed-call build, and the
speed/shipping cost screen has 216 comparison rows against the pre-call-change
control. Both use three alternating windows on CPU0/16 and unchanged full
workload/sample/check settings. Execution/resource counters match throughout.
CPU0 speed compiled-Off integer returns to pre-call-change timing (direct
control/candidate 0.9999); CPU16 is 1.0556. However, CPU0 shipping float regresses
(0.9540), native array on CPU16 is 0.9678 versus the fixed-call build, and other
gates still fail. Faster no-feature observations are not evidence of lower JIT
feature overhead. The CPU16 no-feature integer control has a broad timing range;
do not treat its large ratio as a certified optimization gain. All 36 aggregate
commands fail. No new overall performance or shipping acceptance is claimed.

Evidence: `target/jit-evidence/short-slice-performance/fixed-call-cost-profile/`
contains exact-image profiles/assembly, and `signed-offset-*` contains the fix,
validation, native screen, cost screen, hashes and telemetry. Physical-call
optimization remains WIP; the full plan and all other open gates remain open.

#### Fixed-capacity physical calls — measured, unaccepted WIP

The JIT activation host now has an allocation-free fixed-argument closure-call
path. It requires a fresh closure, a non-variable caller, sufficient value/frame
capacity, arguments within the fixed parameter/register bounds, and room below
the depth limit. It moves arguments and initializes the remaining registers in
place, preserving the real callee frame, caller PC/return expectation, shared
VM fuel constants and interpreter dispatch accounting. Refusal has no effects;
allocation, excess arguments, depth limits and other calls stay on the original
path. Ordinary VM and no-feature execution sources are otherwise unchanged.

Initial focused validation passed 101 executions. Expanded validation passed
52 focused executions and 1,324 full GNU all-feature Auto executions (six
ignored). Two dedicated physical-call differential tests pass Memcheck with
zero errors and zero definite/indirect leaks; harness reports retain 48 possibly
lost and 632 reachable bytes. Cases include missing/excess arguments, zero-width
frames, frame/value capacity refusal, depth errors and saturated/interrupted
fuel. Native call, alias, error and panic tests remain enabled.

Two frozen native screens each contain 324 rows: all nine workloads, three
alternating windows per CPU0/CPU16, eleven paired samples and unchanged gates.
The final shared-fuel-constant build improves direct upvalue control/candidate
ratios to **1.0410/1.0457**, with all execution/resource counters identical.
The initial original-flag symbol profile used 276,717,634 instructions versus
294,367,740 for retained control; that profile predates the shared-constant
follow-up and is not a profile of the final executable. Native acceptance still
fails: the upvalue speedup over its own interpreter remains below 1.25.

The final change is **not accepted**. A separate 216-row speed/shipping cost
screen used fresh pre-change and candidate artifacts built at the same repo
path, identical common invocation paths, three alternating windows on both
cores, eleven samples and twenty iterations. No-feature binaries are
byte-identical in both profiles. Speed compiled-Off integer direct ratios are
**0.9119/1.0024**; float ratios are **0.9801/0.9758**, with CPU0 float failures
increasing from 0/3 to 3/3. Shipping timings are broadly near control, but
existing failures remain. All 24 cost gate commands and all 24 native gate
commands failed. No threshold, workload or native coverage requirement changed.

This source remains feature-branch WIP while the new disabled-path regression
is investigated; the native gain alone does not justify release acceptance.
Next inspect the actual speed compiled-Off executable/code generation before
adding layout or inlining hints. Evidence is retained under
`target/jit-evidence/short-slice-performance/in-place-call-*`, especially
`in-place-call-final-screen/` and `in-place-call-cost/screen/`.

The trial made `ThreadState::close_upvalues` check the highest open capture before

index order, so an empty list or highest index below the returning frame means
there is nothing to close. Exact-boundary captures still follow the original
closing path. Frame construction, returned values, capture mutation and fuel
are unchanged. This affects baseline and JIT-enabled runtimes alike.

A new unit matrix covers empty/single/sparse lists, exact boundaries and
`usize::MAX`, then mutates the stack and closes the remaining captures to check
which values remained live. `make vm-upvalue-returns` adds baseline and

executions / sixteen suites**, two ignored. The boundary matrix also passes
Miri Stacked Borrows seed 1 and Tree Borrows seed 2, one test each; these are
Rust capture-state tests, not generated execution in Miri.

screens on CPU0/CPU16 complete **72 checked commands / 1,080 parsed rows**;

artifact hashes match. Profiling and builds finished before timing began.
The targeted function drops from **4,550,715 to 3,120,754** instructions;
whole-profile work drops from **310,777,895 to 309,397,134** (0.44%).

control/candidate ratios are **0.9840 / 0.9856** on CPU0 and **1.0038 / 1.0051**

The boundary regression and Make gates remain; production behavior returns to

The new frozen bridge executable's loaded sections and program headers match
its symbol replay exactly. Its upvalue profile records **310,777,895**

Admitted pairs now invoke physical Call and Return through ordinary Rust

callee. One Rust unwind boundary surrounds the sequence; generated frames never

The code owner retains the callee entry and immutable source-bound operands,
with allocation charging derived from its actual size. All physical-frame,
capture, prototype, fuel and materialization checks remain in place.

Focused backend, canonical and native-region checks pass **104 executions /
seven suites**, two ignored. New direct-path tests
check callback bypass, budget refusal, matching full traces, call errors and
panic transport before native execution and before writeback. Existing custom
callback fault fixtures explicitly retain their aggregate path in test builds;
they are not claimed as coverage of the new direct path. The full source/fuel
matrix additionally compares the Rust bridge with interpreted execution.
Five frozen original-flag binaries and three alternating windows on CPU0 and
CPU16 complete **72 checked commands / 1,080 parsed rows**. All aggregate gates
still fail. Both no-feature binaries are byte-identical to the admitted-callee
control. Twelve complete counter comparisons match exactly except the predicted
**24-byte** retained/peak metadata increase for the upvalue Auto pair; artifact
hashes verify. Builds and tests did not overlap the timing runs.

Native upvalue direct control/candidate ratios are **0.9982 / 1.0051** on CPU0
and **1.0274 / 1.0258** on CPU16: essentially flat on the first core class and
about 2.6% faster on the second. Own-Off/Auto ratios remain **0.7034–0.7769**,

improve to **1.0883 / 1.0911** and **1.0925 / 1.1075**; shipping integers and
upvalues also improve. This disabled-mode effect cannot be attributed to the
new bridge executing, since it is not executed with JIT Off.

Tradeoffs remain: speed-profile CPU0 compiled-Off integer/float timings worsen
about 2–2.5%; CPU16 native array/metamethod results worsen about 4–5% on one
path. The candidate is retained only as **unaccepted experimental work**, not a
resolved regression or accepted tradeoff. GNU baseline, all-feature Auto and
documentation gates pass **1,714 executions / 172 suites**, ten ignored and no
failures, after timing completes. This does not establish a new Off/Force,
musl, ARM64 or generated-code safety-platform matrix. Resolve the new cost and
